required method MeanMethod

Mean estimator — "mean" (arithmetic), "median", "trimmed" (symmetric trimmed mean), or "huber" (iteratively reweighted Huber M-estimator).

'mean' trim_proportion float

Fraction cut from each tail for method="trimmed"; must satisfy 0 <= p < 0.5.

0.1 huber_c float

Huber tuning constant in robust z-score units for method="huber"; smaller values down-weight outliers more aggressively. Must be positive.

1.345 axis int

Position of the spectral axis. Default -3.

-3

Returns:

Type Description Float[ndarray, ' c']

Mean spectrum with one entry per band, fitted on valid pixels

Float[ndarray, ' c']

only (pixels with any non-finite band are ignored).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If method is unknown, trim_proportion is out of range, or huber_c is not positive.

Source code in packages/geotoolz-ops/src/geoops/matched_filter/_src/array.py 
def estimate_mean(
    cube: Float[np.ndarray, "c h w"],
    *,
    method: MeanMethod = "mean",
    trim_proportion: float = 0.1,
    huber_c: float = 1.345,
    axis: int = -3,
) -> Float[np.ndarray, " c"]:
    """Estimate a per-band background mean spectrum from a cube.

    Robustness matters for matched filtering: sparse bright targets
    (plumes, panels) bias the plain mean toward the target itself, so
    the ``median``, ``trimmed``, or ``huber`` estimators usually give a
    cleaner background.

    Args:
        cube: Spectral cube, canonically ``(c, h, w)``; any number of
            non-band dimensions is supported.
        method: Mean estimator — ``"mean"`` (arithmetic), ``"median"``,
            ``"trimmed"`` (symmetric trimmed mean), or ``"huber"``
            (iteratively reweighted Huber M-estimator).
        trim_proportion: Fraction cut from *each* tail for
            ``method="trimmed"``; must satisfy ``0 <= p < 0.5``.
        huber_c: Huber tuning constant in robust z-score units for
            ``method="huber"``; smaller values down-weight outliers more
            aggressively. Must be positive.
        axis: Position of the spectral axis. Default ``-3``.

    Returns:
        Mean spectrum with one entry per band, fitted on valid pixels
        only (pixels with any non-finite band are ignored).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``method`` is unknown, ``trim_proportion`` is out
            of range, or ``huber_c`` is not positive.
    """
    x = _finite_rows(_cube_samples(cube, axis)[0])
    if method == "mean":
        return np.mean(x, axis=0)
    if method == "median":
        return np.median(x, axis=0)
    if method == "trimmed":
        if not 0 <= trim_proportion < 0.5:
            raise ValueError("trim_proportion must satisfy 0 <= p < 0.5")
        return stats.trim_mean(x, proportiontocut=trim_proportion, axis=0)
    if method == "huber":
        return _huber_mean(x, c=huber_c)
    raise ValueError(f"unknown mean method {method!r}")

Return the theoretical matched-filter detection SNR.

For a target of amplitude a in Gaussian background noise with covariance :math:\Sigma, the matched-filter output SNR is :math:a \sqrt{t^\top \Sigma^{-1} t}.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

Source code in packages/geotoolz-ops/src/geoops/matched_filter/_src/array.py 
def matched_filter_snr(
    *,
    amplitude: float,
    cov_op: NumpyLinearOperator | Float[np.ndarray, "c c"],
    target: Float[np.ndarray, " c"],
) -> float:
    """Return the theoretical matched-filter detection SNR.

    For a target of amplitude ``a`` in Gaussian background noise with
    covariance :math:`\\Sigma`, the matched-filter output SNR is
    :math:`a \\sqrt{t^\\top \\Sigma^{-1} t}`.

    Args:
        amplitude: Target amplitude ``a``.
        cov_op: Background covariance as a `NumpyLinearOperator` or a
            raw ``(c, c)`` matrix.
        target: Target signature ``(c,)``.

    Returns:
        The scalar SNR.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the target/covariance pair produces a
            non-positive filter gain.
    """
    t = np.asarray(target, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
    gain = float(t @ solve(cov_op, t))
    if not np.isfinite(gain) or gain <= 0:
        raise ValueError("target/covariance produce a non-positive MF gain")
    return float(amplitude) * float(np.sqrt(gain))

docs.title: shrink_covariance(empirical, *, method, n_samples, fourth_moment=None)
docs.text:
Shrink an empirical covariance toward a scaled-identity target.

Returns the convex combination (1 − s)·S + s·F with target F = μ·I, μ = tr(S)/p, where S is the ddof=1 sample covariance of n samples in p bands and the intensity s ∈ [0, 1] is estimated from the data. Both estimators reproduce scikit-learn exactly: with the 1/n scatter Sₙ = S·(n − 1)/n (sklearn's empirical_covariance), s is sklearn's shrinkage and the result is n/(n − 1) times sklearn's shrunk matrix (the intensity is scale-free, the target scales with S).

  • "ledoit_wolf" (Ledoit & Wolf 2004, sklearn's ledoit_wolf_shrinkage), with dₖ = xₖ − x̄ the centred samples and m₄ = (1/n) Σₖ ‖dₖ‖⁴::

    δ² = ‖Sₙ − μₙ I‖²_F (distance to target) β̄² = (1/n²) Σₖ ‖dₖdₖᵀ − Sₙ‖²_F = (m₄ − ‖Sₙ‖²_F) / n s = min(β̄², δ²) / δ² (0 when δ² = 0)

β̄² is the sample variance of the entries of Sₙ; it needs the fourth moment m₄, which cannot be recovered from S alone.

  • "oas" (Chen et al. 2010, as implemented by sklearn.covariance.oas)::

    s = min(1, (tr(S²) + tr(S)²) / ((n + 1)·(tr(S²) − tr(S)²/p)))

sklearn omits the 2/p terms of Chen et al. Eq. 23, ((1 − 2/p)·tr(S²) + tr(S)²) / ((n + 1 − 2/p)·(…)); they vanish for large p and are omitted here too so the two agree exactly.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default empirical Float[ndarray, 'c c']

ddof=1 empirical covariance matrix (c, c) (Σ dₖdₖᵀ / max(n − 1, 1)).

required method CovShrinkageMethod

Shrinkage-intensity estimator.

required n_samples int

Number of samples used to form empirical; more samples mean less shrinkage.

required fourth_moment float | None

m₄ = (1/n) Σₖ ‖xₖ − x̄‖⁴ over the same centred samples. Required for method="ledoit_wolf" (ignored by "oas"); WelfordAccumulator tracks it as m4 / count. estimate_cov_shrunk computes it for you from a cube.

None

Returns:

Type Description Float[ndarray, 'c c']

The shrunk (c, c) covariance matrix.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If method is unknown or fourth_moment is missing for "ledoit_wolf".

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> x = np.random.default_rng(0).normal(size=(30, 4))
>>> d = x - x.mean(axis=0)
>>> s = d.T @ d / 29
>>> m4 = float(np.mean(np.sum(d * d, axis=1) ** 2))
>>> shrink_covariance(s, method="ledoit_wolf", n_samples=30,
...                   fourth_moment=m4).shape
(4, 4)
>>> shrink_covariance(s, method="oas", n_samples=30).shape
(4, 4)
Source code in packages/geotoolz-ops/src/geoops/matched_filter/_src/array.py 
def shrink_covariance(
    empirical: Float[np.ndarray, "c c"],
    *,
    method: CovShrinkageMethod,
    n_samples: int,
    fourth_moment: float | None = None,
) -> Float[np.ndarray, "c c"]:
    """Shrink an empirical covariance toward a scaled-identity target.

    Returns the convex combination ``(1 − s)·S + s·F`` with target
    ``F = μ·I``, ``μ = tr(S)/p``, where ``S`` is the ``ddof=1`` sample
    covariance of ``n`` samples in ``p`` bands and the intensity
    ``s ∈ [0, 1]`` is estimated from the data. Both estimators reproduce
    scikit-learn exactly: with the ``1/n`` scatter ``Sₙ = S·(n − 1)/n``
    (sklearn's ``empirical_covariance``), ``s`` is sklearn's shrinkage
    and the result is ``n/(n − 1)`` times sklearn's shrunk matrix (the
    intensity is scale-free, the target scales with ``S``).

    - ``"ledoit_wolf"`` (Ledoit & Wolf 2004, sklearn's
      ``ledoit_wolf_shrinkage``), with ``dₖ = xₖ − x̄`` the centred
      samples and ``m₄ = (1/n) Σₖ ‖dₖ‖⁴``::

          δ² = ‖Sₙ − μₙ I‖²_F                      (distance to target)
          β̄² = (1/n²) Σₖ ‖dₖdₖᵀ − Sₙ‖²_F = (m₄ − ‖Sₙ‖²_F) / n
          s  = min(β̄², δ²) / δ²                    (0 when δ² = 0)

      β̄² is the sample variance of the entries of ``Sₙ``; it needs the
      fourth moment ``m₄``, which cannot be recovered from ``S`` alone.

    - ``"oas"`` (Chen et al. 2010, as implemented by
      ``sklearn.covariance.oas``)::

          s = min(1, (tr(S²) + tr(S)²) / ((n + 1)·(tr(S²) − tr(S)²/p)))

      sklearn omits the ``2/p`` terms of Chen et al. Eq. 23,
      ``((1 − 2/p)·tr(S²) + tr(S)²) / ((n + 1 − 2/p)·(…))``; they vanish
      for large ``p`` and are omitted here too so the two agree exactly.

    Args:
        empirical: ``ddof=1`` empirical covariance matrix ``(c, c)``
            (``Σ dₖdₖᵀ / max(n − 1, 1)``).
        method: Shrinkage-intensity estimator.
        n_samples: Number of samples used to form ``empirical``; more
            samples mean less shrinkage.
        fourth_moment: ``m₄ = (1/n) Σₖ ‖xₖ − x̄‖⁴`` over the same centred
            samples. Required for ``method="ledoit_wolf"`` (ignored by
            ``"oas"``); `WelfordAccumulator` tracks it as ``m4 / count``.
            `estimate_cov_shrunk` computes it for you from a cube.

    Returns:
        The shrunk ``(c, c)`` covariance matrix.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``method`` is unknown or ``fourth_moment`` is
            missing for ``"ledoit_wolf"``.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> x = np.random.default_rng(0).normal(size=(30, 4))
        >>> d = x - x.mean(axis=0)
        >>> s = d.T @ d / 29
        >>> m4 = float(np.mean(np.sum(d * d, axis=1) ** 2))
        >>> shrink_covariance(s, method="ledoit_wolf", n_samples=30,
        ...                   fourth_moment=m4).shape
        (4, 4)
        >>> shrink_covariance(s, method="oas", n_samples=30).shape
        (4, 4)
    """
    cov = np.asarray(empirical, dtype=float)
    n_features = cov.shape[0]
    mu = float(np.trace(cov)) / n_features
    if method == "oas":
        # Scale-free ratio, so S (1/(n−1)) and Sₙ (1/n) give the same s.
        trace_sq = float(np.trace(cov)) ** 2
        fro_sq = float(np.sum(cov * cov))
        denom = (n_samples + 1) * (fro_sq - trace_sq / n_features)
        shrinkage = 1.0 if denom <= 0 else min(1.0, (fro_sq + trace_sq) / denom)
    elif method == "ledoit_wolf":
        if fourth_moment is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "ledoit_wolf shrinkage needs fourth_moment = mean(‖xₖ − x̄‖⁴); "
                "use estimate_cov_shrunk on the samples or WelfordAccumulator.m4"
            )
        n = max(int(n_samples), 1)
        # Sₙ = Σ dₖdₖᵀ / n — the scatter normalisation LW is defined on.
        scatter = cov * (max(n - 1, 1) / n)
        mu_n = float(np.trace(scatter)) / n_features
        diff = scatter - mu_n * np.eye(n_features, dtype=float)
        d_sq = float(np.sum(diff * diff))
        b_bar_sq = max(
            (float(fourth_moment) - float(np.sum(scatter * scatter))) / n, 0.0
        )
        b_sq = min(b_bar_sq, d_sq)
        shrinkage = 0.0 if b_sq == 0 else b_sq / d_sq
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown covariance shrinkage method {method!r}")
    return (1.0 - shrinkage) * cov + shrinkage * mu * np.eye(n_features, dtype=float)

def validate_mf_inputs(
    *,
    cov_op: NumpyLinearOperator | Float[np.ndarray, "c c"],
    target: Float[np.ndarray, " c"],
) -> None:
    """Raise ``ValueError`` for degenerate target/covariance pairs.

    Checks, in order: the target has at least one non-zero entry, the
    covariance system is solvable, and the resulting filter gain
    :math:`t^\\top \\Sigma^{-1} t` is finite and positive.

    Args:
        cov_op: Background covariance as a `NumpyLinearOperator` or a
            raw ``(c, c)`` matrix.
        target: Target signature ``(c,)``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the target is all-zero, the covariance is
            singular, or the filter gain is non-positive.
    """
    t = np.asarray(target, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
    if t.size == 0 or not np.any(t):
        raise ValueError("target must contain at least one non-zero value")
    try:
        gain = float(t @ solve(cov_op, t))
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError as exc:
        raise ValueError("covariance operator must be non-singular") from exc
    if not np.isfinite(gain) or gain <= 0:
        raise ValueError("target/covariance produce a non-positive MF gain")

docs.title: Measure
docs.text:
geoops.measure wraps skimage.measure for region properties and contour extraction. Outputs are either label GeoArrays or GeoDataFrames with geometries in the input CRS.

  • LabelConnectedComponents — component labelling with connectivity=4|8 (skimage's 1|2 spelling is not accepted) and an optional min_area_px filter
  • RegionProps — per-component property table, called as RegionProps()(labels, intensity_image) (the optional intensity image must share the label map's grid); carries forbid_in_yaml=True (extra_properties callables cannot round-trip). Property columns are in pixel units (areas in pixels, lengths in pixel widths, positions as (row, col)); scale_to_crs=True converts areas / lengths / second moments to CRS units. The geometry column is always in CRS units.
  • FindContours — marching-squares iso-contours emitted as LineString features (CRS units)
  • SkeletonLength — longest Euclidean path through the mask skeleton, in pixel widths (scale_to_crs=True for CRS units)
  • ProfileLine — sample values along a line between two points
  • RANSAC — generic model fitting on (N, 2) coordinate pairs
  • ShannonEntropy — single-band scalar entropy

Shared primitives (also used by geoops.mask and geoops.plume): label_components, skeleton_length, regionprops_frame and DEFAULT_REGIONPROPS, plus regionprops_to_crs_units (the scale_to_crs=True conversion).

Wraps :func:skimage.measure.find_contours over a single-band (H, W) or (1, H, W) image and maps each contour's pixel coordinates into world coordinates. Geo-dependent: the output geometries need the carrier's transform/CRS, so the input must be a georeferenced GeoArray (plain arrays raise TypeError).

Units: the geometry column is in CRS units (contour vertices are sub-pixel positions mapped through the transform, pixel centres at integer (row, col)); contour_id is a 1-based index. There are no pixel-unit columns, so there is no scale_to_crs switch.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default level float | None

Iso-value along which to find contours; None uses the midpoint of the image's value range.

None fully_connected str

Whether high- or low-valued pixels are considered fully connected ("low" or "high").

class FindContours(Operator):
    """Extract iso-value contours as LineString geometries.

    Wraps :func:`skimage.measure.find_contours` over a single-band
    ``(H, W)`` or ``(1, H, W)`` image and maps each contour's pixel
    coordinates into world coordinates. Geo-dependent: the output
    geometries need the carrier's transform/CRS, so the input must be a
    georeferenced ``GeoArray`` (plain arrays raise ``TypeError``).

    Units: the ``geometry`` column is in CRS units (contour vertices are
    sub-pixel positions mapped through the transform, pixel centres at
    integer ``(row, col)``); ``contour_id`` is a 1-based index. There are
    no pixel-unit columns, so there is no ``scale_to_crs`` switch.

    Args:
        level: Iso-value along which to find contours; ``None`` uses the
            midpoint of the image's value range.
        fully_connected: Whether high- or low-valued pixels are
            considered fully connected (``"low"`` or ``"high"``).

    Raises:
        TypeError: If the input is not a georeferenced GeoArray.
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy",)
    # marching squares over 2 x 2 cells
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling(
        couples={"space"}, reach=1, kind="conversion"
    )

    _terminal: ClassVar[bool] = True

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        level: float | None = None,
        fully_connected: str = "low",
    ) -> None:
        self.level = level
        self.fully_connected = fully_connected

    def _apply(self, gt: GeoArray) -> gpd.GeoDataFrame:
        LineString = optional_name(
            "shapely.geometry",
            "LineString",
            "vector",
            feature="geoops.measure.FindContours",
        )
        find_contours = optional_name(
            "skimage.measure",
            "find_contours",
            "morph",
            feature="geoops.measure.FindContours",
        )
        gpd = import_optional(
            "geopandas", "vector", feature="geoops.measure.FindContours"
        )
        require_geoarray(gt, "FindContours")
        contours = find_contours(
            single_band(np.asarray(gt, dtype=float), name="FindContours"),
            level=self.level,
            fully_connected=self.fully_connected,
        )
        rows = []
        for contour_id, coords in enumerate(contours, start=1):
            if len(coords) >= 2:
                xs, ys = pixel_xy(gt.transform, coords[:, 0], coords[:, 1])
                geometry = LineString(np.column_stack([xs, ys]))
                rows.append({"contour_id": contour_id, "geometry": geometry})
        if not rows:
            # No contours (constant raster, out-of-range level, or all
            # segments degenerate to <2 points). Return an empty
            # GeoDataFrame with the expected schema instead of letting the
            # constructor raise on a missing ``geometry`` column.
            return gpd.GeoDataFrame(
                {"contour_id": [], "geometry": []},
                geometry="geometry",
                crs=gt.crs,
            )
        return gpd.GeoDataFrame(rows, geometry="geometry", crs=gt.crs)

class LabelConnectedComponents(Operator):
    """Convert a binary mask into an int32 connected-component label map.

    Delegates to :func:`geoops.measure.label_components`. Expects a
    single-band ``(H, W)`` or ``(1, H, W)`` mask; pixels different from
    ``background`` are foreground. Accepts a ``GeoArray`` or a plain
    ``np.ndarray`` and returns an ``int32`` label map (contiguous labels
    ``1..K`` in raster order) in the same carrier kind, with
    ``fill_value=0``. Nodata input pixels (non-finite or equal to
    the input's fill) are background ``0`` and never join components.

    Args:
        connectivity: ``4`` (edge neighbours, default) or ``8`` (edge +
            diagonal neighbours).
        background: Pixel value treated as background and labelled ``0``.
        min_area_px: Minimum component size in pixels; smaller components
            become background. ``0`` keeps every component.
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy",)
    # a connected component can span the scene
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling(couples={"space"}, reach=None)

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        connectivity: Connectivity = 4,
        background: int = 0,
        min_area_px: int = 0,
    ) -> None:
        self.connectivity = connectivity
        self.background = background
        self.min_area_px = min_area_px

    def _apply(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> GeoArray | np.ndarray:
        values = single_band(np.asarray(gt), name="LabelConnectedComponents")
        labels = label_components(
            (values != self.background) & single_band(valid_pixels(gt)),
            connectivity=self.connectivity,
            min_area_px=self.min_area_px,
        )
        return wrap_like(gt, labels, fill_value=0)

class RANSAC(Operator):
    """Robust model fitting via :func:`skimage.measure.ransac`.

    Carrier-agnostic: the input is whatever data layout the chosen model
    class consumes (e.g. an ``(N, D)`` point array), and the output is
    the ``(model, inlier_mask)`` pair returned by ``ransac``.

    Args:
        model_class: skimage model class to fit (e.g.
            ``skimage.measure.LineModelND``). Not YAML-serialisable, so
            instances are forbidden in YAML.
        min_samples: Minimum number of samples per model estimate.
        residual_threshold: Maximum residual for a sample to count as an
            inlier.
        **kwargs: Extra keyword arguments forwarded to
            :func:`skimage.measure.ransac` (e.g. ``max_trials``, ``rng``).
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy",)
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling(kind="conversion")

    _terminal: ClassVar[bool] = True

    forbid_in_yaml: ClassVar[bool] = True

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        model_class: type[Any],
        min_samples: int,
        residual_threshold: float,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> None:
        self.model_class = model_class
        self.min_samples = min_samples
        self.residual_threshold = residual_threshold
        self.kwargs = kwargs

    def _apply(self, data: Any) -> Any:
        ransac = optional_name(
            "skimage.measure",
            "ransac",
            "morph",
            feature="geoops.measure.RANSAC",
        )
        return ransac(
            data,
            self.model_class,
            min_samples=self.min_samples,
            residual_threshold=self.residual_threshold,
            **self.kwargs,
        )

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "model_class": getattr(
                self.model_class,
                "__name__",
                repr(self.model_class),

Bases: Operator

Extract a GeoDataFrame of per-region statistics from a label map.

Wraps :func:skimage.measure.regionprops_table over a single-band (H, W) or (1, H, W) integer label map. When the centroid property is requested (the default), each row carries a Point geometry at the region centroid in world coordinates. Geo-dependent: the output geometry needs the carrier's transform/CRS, so the input must be a georeferenced GeoArray (plain arrays raise TypeError).

The property columns are in pixel units by default -- areas in pixels, lengths (perimeter, major_axis_length, ...) in pixel widths, second moments (inertia_tensor*) in squared pixel widths, positions (centroid-*, bbox-*) as (row, col) indices. With scale_to_crs=True areas, lengths and second moments are converted to CRS units (m^2 / m / m^2 for a projected metric CRS); positions, angles and dimensionless ratios are unchanged.

Called as op(labels, intensity_image=None). The optional intensity_image is a single-band carrier on the label map's pixel grid (ValueError otherwise) and enables intensity-based properties.

class RegionProps(Operator):
    """Extract a GeoDataFrame of per-region statistics from a label map.

    Wraps :func:`skimage.measure.regionprops_table` over a single-band
    ``(H, W)`` or ``(1, H, W)`` integer label map. When the ``centroid``
    property is requested (the default), each row carries a ``Point``
    geometry at the region centroid in world coordinates. Geo-dependent:
    the output geometry needs the carrier's transform/CRS, so the input
    must be a georeferenced ``GeoArray`` (plain arrays raise
    ``TypeError``).

    Units: the ``geometry`` column is in CRS units. The property columns
    are in **pixel units** by default -- areas in pixels, lengths
    (``perimeter``, ``major_axis_length``, ...) in pixel widths, second
    moments (``inertia_tensor*``) in squared pixel widths, positions
    (``centroid-*``, ``bbox-*``) as ``(row, col)`` indices. With
    ``scale_to_crs=True`` areas, lengths and second moments are converted
    to CRS units (m^2 / m / m^2 for a projected metric CRS); positions,
    angles and dimensionless ratios are unchanged.

    Called as ``op(labels, intensity_image=None)``. The optional
    ``intensity_image`` is a single-band carrier on the label map's pixel
    grid (``ValueError`` otherwise) and enables intensity-based
    properties.

    Args:
        properties: Property names passed to ``regionprops_table``;
            defaults to :data:`DEFAULT_REGIONPROPS`.
        extra_properties: Optional callables computing custom per-region
            properties (see skimage docs). Not YAML-serialisable, so
            instances are forbidden in YAML. Their outputs are never
            rescaled.
        scale_to_crs: Convert area / length / second-moment columns from
            pixel to CRS units using the carrier's transform.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If the input is not a georeferenced GeoArray.
        ValueError: If ``intensity_image`` is on another pixel grid, or
            if ``scale_to_crs=True`` and a length or moment
            column is requested on non-square (anisotropic or sheared)
            pixels, where no single pixel length exists.
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy",)
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling(
        couples={"space"}, reach=None, kind="conversion"
    )

    _terminal: ClassVar[bool] = True

    forbid_in_yaml: ClassVar[bool] = True

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        properties: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        extra_properties: Sequence[Callable[..., Any]] | None = None,
        scale_to_crs: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        self.properties = tuple(
            DEFAULT_REGIONPROPS if properties is None else properties
        )
        self.extra_properties = (
            None if extra_properties is None else tuple(extra_properties)
        )
        self.scale_to_crs = scale_to_crs

    def _apply(
        self, gt: GeoArray, intensity_image: GeoArray | np.ndarray | None = None
    ) -> gpd.GeoDataFrame:
        gpd = import_optional(
            "geopandas", "vector", feature="geoops.measure.RegionProps"
        )
        require_geoarray(gt, "RegionProps")
        if intensity_image is not None:
            require_grid_match(
                gt, intensity_image, "RegionProps", names=("labels", "intensity_image")
            )
        labels = single_band(np.asarray(gt), name="RegionProps").astype(
            np.int32, copy=False
        )
        intensity = (
            None
            if intensity_image is None
            else single_band(intensity_image, name="RegionProps intensity_image")
        )
        frame = regionprops_frame(
            labels,
            intensity_image=intensity,
            properties=self.properties,
            extra_properties=self.extra_properties,
        )
        if self.scale_to_crs:
            frame = regionprops_to_crs_units(frame, affine_of(gt))
        if frame.empty:
            return gpd.GeoDataFrame(frame, geometry=[], crs=gt.crs)
        if {"centroid-0", "centroid-1"}.issubset(frame.columns):
            xs, ys = pixel_xy(gt.transform, frame["centroid-0"], frame["centroid-1"])
            geometry = gpd.points_from_xy(xs, ys)
            return gpd.GeoDataFrame(frame, geometry=geometry, crs=gt.crs)
        # Caller omitted centroid: still return a valid GeoDataFrame with an
        # empty (None-valued) geometry column rather than raising in the
        # ``GeoDataFrame`` constructor for missing geometry.
        return gpd.GeoDataFrame(frame, geometry=[None] * len(frame), crs=gt.crs)

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "properties": list(self.properties),
            "extra_properties": None
            if self.extra_properties is None
            else [
                getattr(func, "__name__", repr(func)) for func in self.extra_properties
            ],
            "scale_to_crs": self.scale_to_crs,
        }

docs.title: SkeletonLength
docs.text:
Bases: Operator

Longest path through the skeleton of a binary mask.

Delegates to :func:geoops.measure.skeleton_length: the mask is skeletonised with :func:skimage.morphology.skeletonize and the longest geodesic path through the 8-connected skeleton is measured between pixel centres, each step weighted by its Euclidean length (a diagonal step counts sqrt(2)). This is the geodesic "fiber length" of Pérez Carrasco et al. (2026) with Euclidean rather than unit step weights.

Units: pixel widths by default, so both GeoArray and plain-array carriers are accepted. With scale_to_crs=True steps are measured through the carrier's transform (anisotropic and rotated grids included) and the result is in CRS units (m for a projected metric CRS); the input must then be a georeferenced GeoArray.

Returns 0.0 for empty masks or skeletons that collapse to a single pixel.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default scale_to_crs bool

    length" of Pérez Carrasco et al. (2026) with Euclidean rather than
    unit step weights.

    carriers are accepted. With ``scale_to_crs=True`` steps are measured
    through the carrier's transform (anisotropic and rotated grids
    included) and the result is in CRS units (m for a projected metric
    CRS); the input must then be a georeferenced ``GeoArray``.

    pixel.

            instead of pixel widths.

def label_components(
    mask: Bool[np.ndarray, "h w"],
    *,
    connectivity: Connectivity = 8,
    min_area_px: int = 0,
) -> Int[np.ndarray, "h w"]:
    """Label connected True regions and drop components below ``min_area_px``.

    Uses :func:`scipy.ndimage.label` (raster-order labels, identical to
    :func:`skimage.measure.label` on a boolean mask), then renumbers the
    surviving components contiguously (``1..K``) without a second
    labelling pass -- dropping pixels from a labelled image cannot merge
    distinct components.

    Args:
        mask: 2-D mask; any array-like is coerced with
            ``np.asarray(mask, dtype=bool)``.
        connectivity: ``4`` or ``8`` neighbourhood for component
            membership.
        min_area_px: Minimum component size in pixels; smaller components
            become background. ``0`` and ``1`` keep every component.

    Returns:
        An ``int32`` label image with contiguous labels ``1..K`` for the
        surviving components and ``0`` for background.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``min_area_px`` is negative or ``connectivity`` is
            not 4 or 8.
    """
    if min_area_px < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"min_area_px must be non-negative, got {min_area_px}")
    labels, n_labels = ndimage.label(
        np.asarray(mask, dtype=bool), structure=connectivity_structure(connectivity)
    )
    if n_labels == 0 or min_area_px <= 1:
        return labels.astype(np.int32, copy=False)
    counts = np.bincount(labels.ravel())
    keep = counts >= min_area_px
    keep[0] = False
    # 0..K renumbering LUT so labels stay contiguous after dropping.
    lut = np.zeros_like(counts, dtype=np.int32)
    lut[keep] = np.arange(1, int(keep.sum()) + 1, dtype=np.int32)
    return lut[labels]

Convert pixel-unit region-property columns to CRS units.

With A = |a·e - b·d| the pixel area and s the pixel side:

area → area · A,   length → length · s,   moment → moment · s²

Columns are matched by their base name (inertia_tensor-0-1 → inertia_tensor); unlisted columns are copied unchanged.

Parameters:

required transform Any

Type Description DataFrame

A converted copy of frame.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If a length or moment column is present and the pixels are not square (anisotropic or sheared), where no single pixel length exists.

Examples:

>>> from affine import Affine
>>> frame = pd.DataFrame({"label": [1], "area": [4.0], "perimeter": [8.0]})
>>> regionprops_to_crs_units(frame, Affine(10, 0, 0, 0, -10, 0))
   label   area  perimeter
0      1  400.0       80.0
Source code in packages/geotoolz-ops/src/geoops/measure/_src/array.py 
def regionprops_to_crs_units(frame: pd.DataFrame, transform: Any) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Convert pixel-unit region-property columns to CRS units.

    With ``A = |a·e - b·d|`` the pixel area and ``s`` the pixel side:

        area → area · A,   length → length · s,   moment → moment · s²

    Columns are matched by their base name (``inertia_tensor-0-1`` →
    ``inertia_tensor``); unlisted columns are copied unchanged.

    Args:
        frame: A :func:`regionprops_frame` table in pixel units.
        transform: Affine-like object exposing ``a, b, d, e``.

    Returns:
        A converted copy of ``frame``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a length or moment column is present and the
            pixels are not square (anisotropic or sheared), where no
            single pixel length exists.

    Examples:
        >>> from affine import Affine
        >>> frame = pd.DataFrame({"label": [1], "area": [4.0], "perimeter": [8.0]})
        >>> regionprops_to_crs_units(frame, Affine(10, 0, 0, 0, -10, 0))
           label   area  perimeter
        0      1  400.0       80.0
    """
    a, b = float(transform.a), float(transform.b)
    d, e = float(transform.d), float(transform.e)
    pixel_area = abs(a * e - b * d)
    # Transform columns: the CRS step of one pixel column / row.
    col_step, row_step = float(np.hypot(a, d)), float(np.hypot(b, e))
    square = bool(
        np.isclose(col_step, row_step)
        and np.isclose(a * b + d * e, 0.0, atol=1e-12 * max(pixel_area, 1.0))
    )
    out = frame.copy()
    for column in frame.columns:
        base = str(column).split("-")[0]
        if base in AREA_PROPS:
            out[column] = frame[column] * pixel_area
        elif base in LENGTH_PROPS or base in MOMENT_PROPS:
            if not square:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"RegionProps(scale_to_crs=True): {base!r} has no CRS-unit "
                    f"equivalent on non-square pixels (transform a={a}, b={b}, "
                    f"d={d}, e={e}); request area properties only, or resample "
                    "to square pixels first."
                )
            power = 1 if base in LENGTH_PROPS else 2
            out[column] = frame[column] * col_step**power
    return out

docs.title: skeleton_length(mask, *, step=(1.0, 1.0), connectivity=8)
docs.text:
Longest geodesic path through the skeleton of a binary mask.

The mask is skeletonised with :func:skimage.morphology.skeletonize and each step between neighbouring skeleton pixels is weighted by its Euclidean length, so a diagonal step on square unit pixels counts sqrt(2) and anisotropic / rotated grids are measured correctly. The path runs between skeleton pixel centres: a straight line of n pixels measures n - 1 steps.

The result is the exact graph diameter of each connected skeleton component (the longest of its shortest paths), maximised over components. A tree-shaped component uses a double Dijkstra sweep (farthest pixel from a seed, then farthest from that), which is exact for trees; a component with a loop -- where that sweep can under-estimate -- runs Dijkstra from every pixel. The sweep seed is the lexicographically smallest (row, col), so the result is deterministic.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mask Shaped[ndarray, 'h w']

2-D mask. Boolean input is used as is; other dtypes are foreground where > 0 (NaN is background).

required step tuple[float, float] | Any

Pixel size, either a (dy, dx) pair (row step, column step) or an affine geotransform with a, b, d, e coefficients. The default (1.0, 1.0) returns the length in pixel widths; a geotransform returns it in CRS units (m for a projected metric CRS).

(1.0, 1.0) connectivity Connectivity

8 (default) walks diagonal steps too; 4 walks only edge steps.

8

Returns:

Type Description float

The longest path length in the units of step; 0.0 for an

float

empty mask or when every skeleton component is a single pixel.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If connectivity is not 4 or 8.

Source code in packages/geotoolz-ops/src/geoops/_src/labels.py 
def skeleton_length(
    mask: Shaped[np.ndarray, "h w"],
    *,
    step: tuple[float, float] | Any = (1.0, 1.0),
    connectivity: Connectivity = 8,
) -> float:
    """Longest geodesic path through the skeleton of a binary mask.

    The mask is skeletonised with :func:`skimage.morphology.skeletonize`
    and each step between neighbouring skeleton pixels is weighted by its
    Euclidean length, so a diagonal step on square unit pixels counts
    ``sqrt(2)`` and anisotropic / rotated grids are measured correctly.
    The path runs between skeleton pixel *centres*: a straight line of
    ``n`` pixels measures ``n - 1`` steps.

    The result is the exact graph diameter of each connected skeleton
    component (the longest of its shortest paths), maximised over
    components. A tree-shaped component uses a double Dijkstra sweep
    (farthest pixel from a seed, then farthest from that), which is exact
    for trees; a component with a loop -- where that sweep can
    under-estimate -- runs Dijkstra from every pixel. The sweep seed is
    the lexicographically smallest ``(row, col)``, so the result is
    deterministic.

    Args:
        mask: 2-D mask. Boolean input is used as is; other dtypes are
            foreground where ``> 0`` (``NaN`` is background).
        step: Pixel size, either a ``(dy, dx)`` pair (row step, column
            step) or an affine geotransform with ``a``, ``b``, ``d``,
            ``e`` coefficients. The default ``(1.0, 1.0)`` returns the
            length in pixel widths; a geotransform returns it in CRS
            units (m for a projected metric CRS).
        connectivity: ``8`` (default) walks diagonal steps too; ``4``
            walks only edge steps.

    Returns:
        The longest path length in the units of ``step``; ``0.0`` for an
        empty mask or when every skeleton component is a single pixel.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``connectivity`` is not 4 or 8.
    """
    skeletonize = optional_name(
        "skimage.morphology",
        "skeletonize",
        "morph",
        feature="geoops",
    )
    arr = np.asarray(mask)
    binary = arr if arr.dtype == bool else np.nan_to_num(arr, nan=0.0) > 0
    if connectivity not in (4, 8):
        raise ValueError(f"connectivity must be 4 or 8, got {connectivity!r}")
    if not binary.any():
        return 0.0
    if hasattr(step, "a"):
        a, b, d, e = float(step.a), float(step.b), float(step.d), float(step.e)
    else:
        dy, dx = (float(s) for s in step)
        a, b, d, e = dx, 0.0, 0.0, dy
    # Step length for each (drow, dcol) offset: the transform maps a
    # (dcol, drow) pixel step to (step_x, step_y).
    offsets = _NEIGHBOURS_8 if connectivity == 8 else _NEIGHBOURS_4
    step_length = {
        (drow, dcol): float(np.hypot(a * dcol + b * drow, d * dcol + e * drow))
        for drow, dcol in offsets
    }
    return _longest_path(skeletonize(binary), step_length)

docs.title: Normalize
docs.text:
Per-band scaling and contrast operators for model inputs and display.

  • Per-band scalers: StandardScaler (z-score), RobustScaler (median / IQR), MinMaxScaler, ZeroOne
  • Fixed statistics: Normalize (z-score with given per-band mean / std), PerBandStats (compute and cache NaN-aware per-band statistics)
  • Non-linear scaling: LogScale, AsinhScale, PowerScale
  • Contrast / histogram: HistogramStretch, HistogramMatch, CLAHE
  • Tier-A primitives: standard_scale, robust_scale, minmax_scale (and their inverses inverse_standard_scale, inverse_robust_scale, inverse_minmax_scale), log_scale, asinh_scale, power_scale, histogram_match, reference_cdf, match_cdf, clahe, per_band_stats
  • Per-band statistics on every backend: band_stats, band_quantiles (arrays, band axis by position) and carrier_band_stats (a carrier, band dim by name), mask-aware on NumPy, JAX (under jax.jit too) and dask

See the Normalization guide for when to use which.

class CLAHE(Operator):
    """Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization.

    Reproduces :func:`skimage.exposure.equalize_adapthist` (through
    `clahe`, without scikit-image) independently per band for
    ``(C, H, W)`` carriers while preserving NaN positions and GeoArray
    metadata. Nodata (fill / non-finite) pixels are excluded from the
    histograms and hold the output fill.

    Backends: NumPy, JAX (under ``jax.jit`` too) and dask, where each
    frame's whole ``(band, y, x)`` cube is one task: the tiles need every
    pixel, so a spatially chunked cube is rechunked per frame.

    Args:
        window: Contextual-region shape for the local histograms.
            ``None`` uses scikit-image's default (1/8 of the image height /
            width). Lists (e.g. from Hydra / OmegaConf round-trips)
            are normalised to tuples.
        clip_limit: Contrast-limiting clip threshold in ``[0, 1]``.
            Default ``0.01``.
        nbins: Number of histogram bins. Default ``256``.

    Examples:
        >>> from geoops.normalize import CLAHE
        >>> out = CLAHE(window=(8, 8), clip_limit=0.03)(scene)
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy", "jax", "dask")
    # contextual histograms, on intensities rescaled over the scene
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling(couples={"space"}, reach=None)

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        window: int | tuple[int, int] | list[int] | None = None,
        clip_limit: float = 0.01,
        nbins: int = 256,
    ) -> None:
        # Accept list inputs (e.g. round-trips through Hydra/OmegaConf,
        # which materialise sequences as lists) and normalise to tuple
        # so `clahe` receives its expected type.
        if isinstance(window, list):
            window = tuple(window)
        self.window = window
        self.clip_limit = clip_limit
        self.nbins = nbins

    def _apply(self, gt: Any) -> Any:
        carrier, unwrap = named(gt, name="CLAHE")
        banded = "band" in tuple(get_adapter(carrier).dims(carrier))
        # the whole (band, y, x) cube of a frame in one call: tiles need every
        # pixel, and the pixel rule every band (one dask task per frame)
        op = KernelOp(
            _clahe_kernel,
            "(c,y,x)->(c,y,x)" if banded else "(y,x)->(y,x)",
            core={"c": "band", "y": "y", "x": "x"} if banded else {"y": "y", "x": "x"},
            params={
                "fill": fill_of(carrier),
                "banded": banded,
                "window": self.window,
                "clip_limit": self.clip_limit,
                "nbins": self.nbins,
            },
        )
        return unwrap(_declare_fill(op(carrier), np.nan))

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if isinstance(self.window, tuple):
            window: int | list[int] | None = list(self.window)
        else:
            window = self.window
        return {
            "window": window,
            "clip_limit": self.clip_limit,
            "nbins": self.nbins,
        }

Bases: Operator

Match a GeoArray histogram to a reference GeoArray.

Reshapes the per-band empirical CDF of the input to match the reference. Useful for visual harmonisation across scenes acquired under different illumination. Nodata (fill / non-finite) pixels of both the input and the reference are excluded from the CDFs; input nodata pixels hold the output fill value.

A (T, C, H, W) stack is matched per band with one CDF pooled over every frame (like the module's other fitted statistics), so the relative brightness of the frames survives the matching; a 4-D reference likewise pools its frames per band.

The reference is a live GeoArray — not JSON / YAML serialisable — so forbid_in_yaml = True.

Backends: exact rank matching (reference_cdf, then match_cdf: a sort and searchsorted, the same result as scikit-image's match_histograms) with static shapes, so it runs on NumPy, on JAX under jax.jit (the reference's table is a constant), and lazily on dask, where each band of the source is gathered into one block.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default reference GeoArray | ndarray

Reference GeoArray whose per-band CDF the input will be matched against.

required

Examples:

>>> from geoops.normalize import HistogramMatch
>>> op = HistogramMatch(reference=reference_scene)
>>> matched = op(source_scene)

class HistogramMatch(Operator):
    """Match a GeoArray histogram to a reference GeoArray.

    Reshapes the per-band empirical CDF of the input to match the
    reference. Useful for visual harmonisation across scenes acquired
    under different illumination. Nodata (fill / non-finite) pixels of
    both the input and the reference are excluded from the CDFs; input
    nodata pixels hold the output fill value.

    A ``(T, C, H, W)`` stack is matched per band with one CDF pooled over
    every frame (like the module's other fitted statistics), so the
    relative brightness of the frames survives the matching; a 4-D
    reference likewise pools its frames per band.

    The reference is a live GeoArray — not JSON / YAML serialisable —
    so ``forbid_in_yaml = True``.

    Backends: exact rank matching (`reference_cdf`, then `match_cdf`: a sort
    and ``searchsorted``, the same result as scikit-image's
    ``match_histograms``) with static shapes, so it runs on NumPy, on JAX
    under ``jax.jit`` (the reference's table is a constant), and lazily on
    dask, where each band of the source is gathered into one block.

    Args:
        reference: Reference GeoArray whose per-band CDF the input
            will be matched against.

    Examples:
        >>> from geoops.normalize import HistogramMatch
        >>> op = HistogramMatch(reference=reference_scene)
        >>> matched = op(source_scene)
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy", "jax", "dask")
    # the source CDF of each band over every pixel and frame
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling(couples={"space", "time"}, reach=None)

    # Holds a live GeoArray reference, which is not JSON/YAML
    # serialisable.
    forbid_in_yaml: ClassVar[bool] = True

    def __init__(self, *, reference: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> None:
        self.reference = reference

    def _apply(self, gt: Any) -> Any:
        reject_geotensor(self.reference, "HistogramMatch (reference)")
        source = _pixel_view(gt, "band", "HistogramMatch")
        reference = self.reference
        if isinstance(reference, GeoArray) and reference.backend == "jax":
            # the table is a host constant: build it before any trace sees it
            reference = reference.to_numpy()
        ref = _pixel_view(reference, "band", "HistogramMatch (reference)")
        n_bands = (
            source.data.shape[source.band_axis] if source.band_axis is not None else 1
        )
        ref_bands = ref.data.shape[ref.band_axis] if ref.band_axis is not None else 1
        # per band when the reference has the source's bands or is one 2-D map;
        # otherwise one CDF pooled over every band of each, as before
        per_band = source.band_axis is not None and (
            ref.band_axis is None or ref_bands == n_bands
        )
        _, ref_rows, ref_valid = _as_rows(ref, per_band and ref.band_axis is not None)
        table = reference_cdf(np.asarray(ref_rows), np.asarray(ref_valid))
        if table[0].shape[0] == 1 and per_band:  # one 2-D map for every band
            table = tuple(np.repeat(t, n_bands, axis=0) for t in table)
        xp, rows, valid = _as_rows(source, per_band)
        if xp.__name__ == "dask.array":
            # every pixel of a band in one block, as band_quantiles does
            rows = rows.rechunk({0: 1, 1: -1})
            valid = valid.rechunk({0: 1, 1: -1})
            parts = [xp.from_array(t, chunks=(1, -1)) for t in table]
            matched = xp.map_blocks(match_cdf, rows, valid, *parts, dtype=float)
        else:
            matched = match_cdf(rows, valid, *table)
        return _from_rows(source, xp.where(valid, matched, xp.nan))

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        # Debug payload: the reference is a runtime raster (forbid_in_yaml).
        reference = np.asarray(self.reference)
        return {
            "reference": {
                "shape": list(reference.shape),
                "dtype": str(reference.dtype),
            }
        }

class HistogramStretch(Operator):
    r"""Per-band percentile stretch into ``out_range`` for visualisation.

    Lighter-weight cousin of :class:`geoops.radiometry.PercentileClip`
    (same shared percentile stretch, same ``lower`` / ``upper``
    vocabulary): clips to ``[P_lower, P_upper]`` using NaN-aware
    percentiles, then maps the result into ``out_range`` instead of
    fixed ``[0, 1]``. Percentiles follow the ``normalize`` per-band
    statistics convention: per band, pooled over the frames of a
    ``(T, C, H, W)`` stack (``PercentileClip`` stretches each frame
    independently by default). Nodata (fill / non-finite) pixels are
    excluded from the percentiles and hold the output fill value.

    Args:
        out_range: Two-element increasing tuple. Default
            ``(0.0, 1.0)``.
        lower: Lower percentile. Default ``2.0``.
        upper: Upper percentile. Default ``98.0``; must exceed ``lower``.

    Examples:
        >>> from geoops.normalize import HistogramStretch
        >>> # Standard "satellite RGB to display byte range" stretch.
        >>> op = HistogramStretch(out_range=(0.0, 255.0))
        >>> display = op(reflectance_scene)
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy", "jax", "dask")
    # per-band percentiles over every pixel and frame of the input
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling(couples={"space", "time"}, reach=None)

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        out_range: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 1.0),
        lower: float = 2.0,
        upper: float = 98.0,
    ) -> None:
        self.out_range = validate_out_range(tuple(out_range))
        self.lower = lower
        self.upper = upper

    def _apply(self, gt: Any) -> Any:
        check_percentiles(self.lower, self.upper)
        q = (self.lower / 100.0, self.upper / 100.0)
        lo, hi = _scene_stats(gt, stats=(), quantiles=q)["quantiles"]
        # the band dim is last inside the kernel, so (C,) bounds broadcast as is
        return pixel_kernel(
            _stretch_kernel,
            gt,
            dim="band",
            name="HistogramStretch",
            lo=lo,
            hi=hi,
            out_range=self.out_range,
        )

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "out_range": list(self.out_range),
            "lower": self.lower,
            "upper": self.upper,
        }

class MinMaxScaler(Operator):
    r"""Per-band min-max scaling into an arbitrary output range.

    .. math::

        y \;=\; \frac{x - v_{\min}}{v_{\max} - v_{\min}}
                \cdot (o_{\max} - o_{\min}) + o_{\min}

    Per-band variant of :class:`geoops.radiometry.MinMaxStretch`. The
    radiometry version takes **scalar** bounds and is the display-prep
    pick when you already know fixed reflectance limits; this version
    fits **per-band** bounds (one ``vmin`` / ``vmax`` per channel) or
    accepts cached training-time bounds for inference. When
    ``vmax == vmin`` for a band the divisor falls back to ``1``. Nodata
    (fill / non-finite) pixels are excluded from the fit and hold the
    output fill value.

    Fitted operator with the same ``fit`` / ``transform`` / ``inverse``
    contract as :class:`StandardScaler` (fitted state ``vmin_`` /
    ``vmax_``, never part of ``get_config()``).

    Args:
        vmin: Per-band lower bound, scalar / list / ndarray, or
            ``None`` to fit.
        vmax: Per-band upper bound.
        out_range: ``(out_min, out_max)`` range to map into. Default
            ``(0.0, 1.0)``.
        fit_on_call: If ``True`` and the operator is not fitted yet, fit
            the bounds on the first call and reuse them afterwards.

    Attributes:
        vmin_: Fitted per-band lower bound, or ``None`` before :meth:`fit`.
        vmax_: Fitted per-band upper bound, or ``None`` before :meth:`fit`.

    Examples:
        >>> from geoops.normalize import MinMaxScaler
        >>> # Map per-band [vmin, vmax] into [0, 1]:
        >>> op = MinMaxScaler(vmin=[0.0, 0.0], vmax=[0.3, 0.4])
        >>> scaled = op(scene)
        >>>
        >>> # Or fit on the scene and emit a uint8-style range:
        >>> op = MinMaxScaler(out_range=(0.0, 255.0)).fit(scene)
        >>> display = op(scene)
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy", "jax", "dask")
    # min and max fitted over every pixel and frame
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling(fit={"space", "time"})

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        vmin: np.ndarray | list[float] | float | None = None,
        vmax: np.ndarray | list[float] | float | None = None,
        out_range: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 1.0),
        fit_on_call: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        self.vmin = _array_or_none(vmin)
        self.vmax = _array_or_none(vmax)
        self.out_range = validate_out_range(tuple(out_range))
        self.fit_on_call = fit_on_call
        self.vmin_: np.ndarray | None = None
        self.vmax_: np.ndarray | None = None

    def fit(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> Self:
        """Learn per-band ``vmin_`` / ``vmax_`` from the valid pixels of ``gt``.

        Returns:
            This operator, for chaining.
        """
        stats = _fit_stats(self, gt, stats=("min", "max"))
        self.vmax_ = stats["max"]
        self.vmin_ = stats["min"]  # published last: fit_once checks ``vmin_``
        return self

    def _stats(self) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        if self.vmin_ is not None and self.vmax_ is not None:
            return self.vmin_, self.vmax_
        if self.vmin is not None and self.vmax is not None:
            return self.vmin, self.vmax
        raise ValueError("MinMaxScaler requires vmin/vmax, fit(), or fit_on_call=True")

    def transform(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> GeoArray | np.ndarray:
        """Map ``gt`` from the fitted (or constructor) bounds into ``out_range``."""
        vmin, vmax = self._stats()
        _check_per_band(vmin, gt)
        _check_per_band(vmax, gt)
        return pixel_kernel(
            minmax_scale,
            gt,
            dim="band",
            name="MinMaxScaler",
            vmin=vmin,
            vmax=vmax,
            out_range=self.out_range,
            reduce_axes=None,
        )

    def _apply(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> GeoArray | np.ndarray:
        if self.fit_on_call:
            fit_once(self, gt, lambda: self.vmin_ is not None)
        return self.transform(gt)

    def inverse(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> GeoArray | np.ndarray:
        """Map ``out_range`` values back to the ``[vmin, vmax]`` input scale."""
        vmin, vmax = self._stats()
        _check_per_band(vmin, gt)
        _check_per_band(vmax, gt)
        return pixel_kernel(
            inverse_minmax_scale,
            gt,
            dim="band",
            name="MinMaxScaler.inverse",
            vmin=vmin,
            vmax=vmax,
            out_range=self.out_range,
            reduce_axes=None,
        )

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "vmin": jsonable(self.vmin),
            "vmax": jsonable(self.vmax),
            "out_range": list(self.out_range),
            "fit_on_call": self.fit_on_call,
        }

Compute NaN-aware per-band statistics and cache them.

Side-effect-only operator: returns the input unchanged after caching a stats dict containing per-band mean, std, min, max, and percentiles over the spatial (H, W) axes. >>> op = PerBandStats(percentiles=[2.0, 98.0])
>>> _ = op(scene)
>>> op.stats["mean"]   # one entry per band
[...]

class PerBandStats(Operator):
    """Compute NaN-aware per-band statistics and cache them.

    Side-effect-only operator: returns the input unchanged after caching
    a ``stats`` dict containing per-band ``mean``, ``std``, ``min``,
    ``max``, and ``percentiles`` over the spatial ``(H, W)`` axes. Use
    this in a ``Tap``-style stage to inspect a scene before applying a
    downstream normaliser. Nodata (fill / non-finite) pixels are
    excluded from every statistic.

    Backends: NumPy, eager JAX and dask, where one compute of the
    statistics (not of the data) runs and the input passes through still
    lazy. Under ``jax.jit`` writing ``self.stats`` would leak tracers, so it
    raises; use `carrier_band_stats` inside a trace instead.

    Args:
        percentiles: Percentiles (in ``[0, 100]``) to cache alongside
            mean/std/min/max. Default ``[1.0, 99.0]``.

    Examples:
        >>> from geoops.normalize import PerBandStats
        >>> op = PerBandStats(percentiles=[2.0, 98.0])
        >>> _ = op(scene)
        >>> op.stats["mean"]   # one entry per band
        [...]
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy", "jax", "dask")
    # returns its input; the statistics are a side effect
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling()
    # writes self.stats: eager on JAX, refused under jax.jit (the contract checks)
    traceable: ClassVar[bool] = False

    def __init__(self, *, percentiles: list[float] | None = None) -> None:
        self.percentiles = [1.0, 99.0] if percentiles is None else list(percentiles)
        self.stats: dict[str, Any] = {}

    def _apply(self, gt: Any) -> Any:
        stats = _host_stats(
            gt,
            "PerBandStats",
            f"Call it eagerly, outside the trace; or use {_FUNCTIONAL}",
            quantiles=tuple(p / 100.0 for p in self.percentiles),
        )
        # no levels gives no "quantiles" entry; keep the old empty list
        stats["percentiles"] = stats.pop("quantiles", np.empty(0))
        self.stats = {key: jsonable(value) for key, value in stats.items()}
        return gt

        median: Per-band median (scalar, list, or ndarray) or ``None``.
        iqr: Per-band IQR (``Q3 - Q1``).
        fit_on_call: If ``True`` and the operator is not fitted yet, fit
            on the first call (the 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles) and
            reuse the statistics afterwards.

    Attributes:
        median_: Fitted per-band median, or ``None`` before :meth:`fit`.
        iqr_: Fitted per-band IQR, or ``None`` before :meth:`fit`.

    Examples:
        >>> from geoops.normalize import RobustScaler
        >>> op = RobustScaler().fit(scene)
        >>> op.median_, op.iqr_
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy", "jax", "dask")
    # median and IQR fitted over every pixel and frame
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling(fit={"space", "time"})

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        median: np.ndarray | list[float] | float | None = None,
        iqr: np.ndarray | list[float] | float | None = None,
        fit_on_call: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        self.median = _array_or_none(median)
        self.iqr = _array_or_none(iqr)
        self.fit_on_call = fit_on_call
        self.median_: np.ndarray | None = None
        self.iqr_: np.ndarray | None = None

    def fit(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> Self:
        """Learn per-band ``median_`` / ``iqr_`` from the valid pixels of ``gt``.

        Returns:
            This operator, for chaining.
        """
        quantiles = (0.25, 0.5, 0.75)
        q25, q50, q75 = _fit_stats(self, gt, stats=(), quantiles=quantiles)["quantiles"]
        self.iqr_ = q75 - q25
        self.median_ = q50  # published last: fit_once checks ``median_``
        return self

    def _stats(self) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        if self.median_ is not None and self.iqr_ is not None:
            return self.median_, self.iqr_
        if self.median is not None and self.iqr is not None:
            return self.median, self.iqr
        raise ValueError("RobustScaler requires median/iqr, fit(), or fit_on_call=True")

    def transform(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> GeoArray | np.ndarray:
        """Scale ``gt`` with the fitted (or constructor) median / IQR."""
        median, iqr = self._stats()
        _check_per_band(median, gt)
        _check_per_band(iqr, gt)
        return pixel_kernel(
            robust_scale,
            gt,
            dim="band",
            name="RobustScaler",
            median=median,
            iqr=iqr,
            reduce_axes=None,
        )

    def _apply(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> GeoArray | np.ndarray:
        if self.fit_on_call:
            fit_once(self, gt, lambda: self.median_ is not None)
        return self.transform(gt)

    def inverse(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> GeoArray | np.ndarray:
        """Invert a previously applied robust scaling (``x = y * iqr + median``)."""
        median, iqr = self._stats()
        _check_per_band(median, gt)
        _check_per_band(iqr, gt)
        return pixel_kernel(
            inverse_robust_scale,
            gt,
            dim="band",
            name="RobustScaler.inverse",
            median=median,
            iqr=iqr,
            reduce_axes=None,
        )

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "median": jsonable(self.median),
            "iqr": jsonable(self.iqr),
            "fit_on_call": self.fit_on_call,
        }

docs.text:
Bases: Operator

Per-band z-score normalisation.

.. math::

y \;=\; \frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}

Statistics reduce over the spatial axes (-2, -1) so a (C, H, W) carrier yields per-band mu / sigma of shape (C,). Pass cached training-set statistics via mean / std for inference, call :meth:fit on a training scene, or set fit_on_call=True to fit on the first scene seen. When sigma == 0 (a constant band) the divisor falls back to 1 so the band collapses to zero instead of producing inf / nan. Nodata (fill / non-finite) pixels are excluded from the fit and hold the output fill value.

Fitted operator (see Fitted operators in the concepts guide): :meth:fit learns mean_ / std_ (which then take precedence over the constructor statistics), :meth:transform applies them without mutating the operator, and :meth:inverse undoes the scaling. Learned statistics are never part of get_config(); to persist them, build StandardScaler(mean=op.mean_, std=op.std_).

Backends: :meth:fit runs on NumPy, eager JAX and dask (one compute of the statistics, not of the data) and always stores host NumPy arrays. Under jax.jit it raises, and so does a first fit_on_call call: fit eagerly, then apply the fitted operator inside the trace, where its statistics are constants. :meth:transform and :meth:inverse run everywhere, lazily on dask.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mean ndarray | list[float] | float | None

Per-band mean (scalar, list, or ndarray) or None.

None std ndarray | list[float] | float | None

Per-band std (scalar, list, or ndarray) or None.

None fit_on_call bool

If True and the operator is not fitted yet, fit mean_ / std_ on the first call and reuse them for every later call. The fit runs once even under concurrent calls (pipekit_ops.ThreadMap), but which scene it sees is then the first to arrive -- call :meth:fit before parallel use for a deterministic fit.

False

Attributes:

Name Type Description mean_ ndarray | None

Fitted per-band mean, or None before :meth:fit.

std_ ndarray | None

Fitted per-band std, or None before :meth:fit.

Examples:

>>> from geoops.normalize import StandardScaler
>>> # Inference: cached per-band statistics from training.
>>> scaler = StandardScaler(mean=[0.1, 0.2], std=[0.05, 0.07])
>>> normed = scaler(scene)
>>>
>>> # Training-time fit, then apply:
>>> fit = StandardScaler().fit(train_scene)
>>> normed = fit(scene)
>>> fit.mean_  # fitted per-band ndarray

class StandardScaler(Operator):
    r"""Per-band z-score normalisation.

    .. math::

        y \;=\; \frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}

    Statistics reduce over the spatial axes ``(-2, -1)`` so a
    ``(C, H, W)`` carrier yields per-band ``mu`` / ``sigma`` of shape
    ``(C,)``. Pass cached training-set statistics via ``mean`` / ``std``
    for inference, call :meth:`fit` on a training scene, or set
    ``fit_on_call=True`` to fit on the first scene seen. When
    ``sigma == 0`` (a constant band) the divisor falls back to ``1`` so
    the band collapses to zero instead of producing ``inf`` / ``nan``.
    Nodata (fill / non-finite) pixels are excluded from the fit and hold
    the output fill value.

    Fitted operator (see *Fitted operators* in the concepts guide):
    :meth:`fit` learns ``mean_`` / ``std_`` (which then take precedence
    over the constructor statistics), :meth:`transform` applies them
    without mutating the operator, and :meth:`inverse` undoes the
    scaling. Learned statistics are never part of ``get_config()``; to
    persist them, build ``StandardScaler(mean=op.mean_, std=op.std_)``.

    Backends: :meth:`fit` runs on NumPy, eager JAX and dask (one compute of
    the statistics, not of the data) and always stores host NumPy arrays.
    Under ``jax.jit`` it raises, and so does a first ``fit_on_call``
    call: fit eagerly, then apply the fitted operator inside the trace,
    where its statistics are constants. :meth:`transform` and
    :meth:`inverse` run everywhere, lazily on dask.

    Args:
        mean: Per-band mean (scalar, list, or ndarray) or ``None``.
        std: Per-band std (scalar, list, or ndarray) or ``None``.
        fit_on_call: If ``True`` and the operator is not fitted yet,
            fit ``mean_`` / ``std_`` on the first call and reuse them for
            every later call. The fit
            runs once even under concurrent calls (``pipekit_ops.ThreadMap``),
            but which scene it sees is then the first to arrive -- call
            :meth:`fit` before parallel use for a deterministic fit.

    Attributes:
        mean_: Fitted per-band mean, or ``None`` before :meth:`fit`.
        std_: Fitted per-band std, or ``None`` before :meth:`fit`.

    Examples:
        >>> from geoops.normalize import StandardScaler
        >>> # Inference: cached per-band statistics from training.
        >>> scaler = StandardScaler(mean=[0.1, 0.2], std=[0.05, 0.07])
        >>> normed = scaler(scene)
        >>>
        >>> # Training-time fit, then apply:
        >>> fit = StandardScaler().fit(train_scene)
        >>> normed = fit(scene)
        >>> fit.mean_  # fitted per-band ndarray
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy", "jax", "dask")
    # x' = (x - mu_c) / sigma_c pointwise; mu_c, sigma_c fitted over every pixel and frame
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling(fit={"space", "time"})

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        mean: np.ndarray | list[float] | float | None = None,
        std: np.ndarray | list[float] | float | None = None,
        fit_on_call: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        self.mean = _array_or_none(mean)
        self.std = _array_or_none(std)
        self.fit_on_call = fit_on_call
        self.mean_: np.ndarray | None = None
        self.std_: np.ndarray | None = None

    def fit(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> Self:
        """Learn per-band ``mean_`` / ``std_`` from the valid pixels of ``gt``.

        Returns:
            This operator, for chaining.
        """
        stats = _fit_stats(self, gt, stats=("mean", "std"))
        self.std_ = stats["std"]
        self.mean_ = stats["mean"]  # published last: fit_once checks ``mean_``
        return self

    def _stats(self) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        if self.mean_ is not None and self.std_ is not None:
            return self.mean_, self.std_
        if self.mean is not None and self.std is not None:
            return self.mean, self.std
        raise ValueError("StandardScaler requires mean/std, fit(), or fit_on_call=True")

    def transform(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> GeoArray | np.ndarray:
        """Z-score ``gt`` with the fitted (or constructor) statistics.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the operator has neither fitted nor constructor
                statistics.
        """
        mean, std = self._stats()
        _check_per_band(mean, gt)
        _check_per_band(std, gt)
        # the band dim is last inside the kernel, so (C,) stats broadcast as is
        return pixel_kernel(
            standard_scale,
            gt,
            dim="band",
            name=type(self).__name__,
            mean=mean,
            std=std,
            reduce_axes=None,
        )

    def _apply(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> GeoArray | np.ndarray:
        if self.fit_on_call:
            fit_once(self, gt, lambda: self.mean_ is not None)
        return self.transform(gt)

    def inverse(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> GeoArray | np.ndarray:
        """Invert a previously applied standard scaling.

        Args:
            gt: Scaled carrier (GeoArray or plain ndarray).

        Returns:
            The un-scaled carrier, same kind as ``gt``; nodata pixels
            hold the output fill value.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the scaler has no statistics yet.
        """
        mean, std = self._stats()
        _check_per_band(mean, gt)
        _check_per_band(std, gt)
        return pixel_kernel(
            inverse_standard_scale,
            gt,
            dim="band",
            name=f"{type(self).__name__}.inverse",
            mean=mean,
            std=std,
            reduce_axes=None,
        )

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "mean": jsonable(self.mean),
            "std": jsonable(self.std),
            "fit_on_call": self.fit_on_call,
        }

def asinh_scale(
    arr: Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"], *, a: float = 1.0
) -> Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"]:
    r"""Apply inverse-hyperbolic-sine scaling.

    .. math::

        y \;=\; \mathrm{asinh}(x / a)

    Linear near zero, logarithmic for ``|x| >> a``; symmetric and
    well-defined for negative values (unlike ``log``).

    check_positive("a", a)
    return array_namespace(arr).asinh(arr / a)

def band_quantiles(
    x: Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"],
    valid: Shaped[np.ndarray, "*dims"] | None = None,
    *,
    band_axis: int | None = BAND_AXIS,
    q: tuple[float, ...] | list[float] = (0.25, 0.5, 0.75),
) -> Float[np.ndarray, "levels ..."]:
    r"""Per-band quantiles of the valid pixels, on any backend.

    :math:`q_c(p)` is the :math:`p`-th quantile (linear interpolation, as
    ``np.nanpercentile``) of the valid elements of band :math:`c`, pooled
    over every axis except ``band_axis``.

    On dask an exact quantile needs every pixel of a band in one block, so
    ``dask.array.nanquantile`` rechunks the reduced axes to a single chunk
    and the band axis to ``"auto"``: a task holds whole bands, as many as fit
    dask's ``array.chunk-size`` (at least one), never the whole cube.

    Args:
        x: Float array with the band axis at ``band_axis``.
        valid: Boolean array broadcasting to ``x``; ``False`` leaves an
            element out. Non-finite elements are always left out; ``None``
            keeps every finite element.
        band_axis: The axis kept; ``None`` gives one quantile per level.
        q: Quantile levels in ``[0, 1]``, static (they fix the output shape).

    Returns:
        ``(len(q), C)`` (or ``(len(q),)`` for ``band_axis=None``) on ``x``'s
        backend; a band without valid elements gives ``NaN``.

    Raises:
        TypeError: ``x`` is a georeader ``GeoTensor``.
        ValueError: A level outside ``[0, 1]``.

    Examples:
        >>> x = np.arange(8.0).reshape(2, 2, 2)  # (C=2, H=2, W=2)
        >>> band_quantiles(x, q=(0.0, 0.5, 1.0))
        array([[0. , 4. ],
               [1.5, 5.5],
               [3. , 7. ]])
        >>> # IQR per band, nodata left out
        >>> lo, hi = band_quantiles(x, x != 0.0, q=(0.25, 0.75))
        >>> (hi - lo).tolist()
        [1.0, 1.5]
    """
    levels = np.asarray(q, dtype=float)
    if levels.ndim != 1 or np.any((levels < 0) | (levels > 1)):
        raise ValueError(f"quantile levels must be a sequence in [0, 1]; got {q}")
    xp, data, axes = _band_reduction(x, valid, band_axis, "band_quantiles")
    return xp.nanquantile(data, xp.asarray(levels, dtype=data.dtype), axis=axes)

docs.text:
Per-band mean, std, min and max of the valid pixels, on any backend.

.. math::

\mu_c \;=\; \frac{1}{|V_c|} \sum_{i \in V_c} x_{c,i}

where :math:V_c is the set of valid elements of band :math:c, pooled over every axis except band_axis (the frames of a (T, C, H, W) stack too), and likewise for std, min and max. def band_stats(
    x: Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"],
    valid: Shaped[np.ndarray, "*dims"] | None = None,
    *,
    band_axis: int | None = BAND_AXIS,
    stats: tuple[str, ...] | list[str] = BAND_STATS,
) -> dict[str, Float[np.ndarray, "*stat"]]:
    r"""Per-band mean, std, min and max of the valid pixels, on any backend.

    .. math::

        \mu_c \;=\; \frac{1}{|V_c|} \sum_{i \in V_c} x_{c,i}

    where :math:`V_c` is the set of valid elements of band :math:`c`, pooled
    over every axis except ``band_axis`` (the frames of a ``(T, C, H, W)``
    stack too), and likewise for ``std``, ``min`` and ``max``. Written on the
    array namespace: NumPy, JAX (under ``jax.jit`` too, one trace per shape)
    and dask, where each statistic is a lazy tree reduction.

    Args:
        x: Float array with the band axis at ``band_axis``.
        valid: Boolean array broadcasting to ``x``; ``False`` leaves an
            element out of every statistic. Non-finite elements are always
            left out; ``None`` keeps every finite element.
        band_axis: The axis kept, one statistic per entry; ``None`` reduces
            globally to scalars.
        stats: Which of ``"mean"``, ``"std"``, ``"min"``, ``"max"`` to compute.

    Returns:
        One array per requested statistic, ``(C,)`` (or scalar for
        ``band_axis=None``), on ``x``'s backend; a band without valid
        elements gives ``NaN``.

    Raises:
        TypeError: ``x`` is a georeader ``GeoTensor``.
        ValueError: An unknown statistic name.

    Examples:
        >>> x = np.array([[[1.0, 3.0]], [[2.0, -9.0]]])  # (C=2, H=1, W=2)
        >>> band_stats(x, x != -9.0, stats=("mean", "max"))
        {'mean': array([2., 2.]), 'max': array([3., 2.])}
        >>> # a (T, C, H, W) stack pools its frames: still one value per band
        >>> band_stats(np.ones((4, 3, 2, 2)), stats=("min",))["min"].shape
        (3,)
        >>> float(band_stats(x, x != -9.0, band_axis=None, stats=("min",))["min"])
        1.0
    """
    unknown = [name for name in stats if name not in BAND_STATS]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown statistics {unknown}; choose from {BAND_STATS}")
    xp, data, axes = _band_reduction(x, valid, band_axis, "band_stats")
    reducers = {
        "mean": xp.nanmean,
        "std": xp.nanstd,
        "min": xp.nanmin,
        "max": xp.nanmax,
    }
    return {name: reducers[name](data, axis=axes) for name in stats}
