def carrier_band_stats(
    x: Any,
    *,
    dim: str = "band",
    per_band: bool = True,
    stats: tuple[str, ...] | list[str] = BAND_STATS,
    quantiles: tuple[float, ...] | list[float] = (),
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Per-band statistics of a carrier's valid pixels, by dim name, on its backend.

    The carrier form of `band_stats` and `band_quantiles`. The band dim is
    found by name, so a ``(time, band, y, x)`` stack pools its frames into
    one ``(C,)`` statistic per band. Nodata follows geoops' pixel rule
    (`geoops._src.valid`): a pixel is invalid in every band when any of its
    bands is non-finite or equals the carrier's fill, judged per frame.

    Args:
        x: A NumPy or JAX `GeoArray` (under ``jax.jit`` too), an
            ``xr.DataArray`` (NumPy or dask), a `DimArray` or a plain 2-D to
            4-D array in the layout ``("time", "band", "y", "x")[-ndim:]``.
        dim: The band dim. A carrier without it gives scalar statistics.
        per_band: ``False`` reduces over every dim, bands too, to scalars
            (the pixel rule still uses ``dim``).
        stats: Names for `band_stats`; ``()`` for none.
        quantiles: Levels in ``[0, 1]`` for `band_quantiles`, returned under
            ``"quantiles"`` as ``(len(quantiles), C)``; ``()`` for none.

    Returns:
        One array per statistic on the data's backend: NumPy, JAX (tracers
        under ``jit``), or lazy dask arrays to compute together
        (``dask.compute(*out.values())``).

    Raises:
        TypeError: ``x`` is a georeader ``GeoTensor``.
        ValueError: An unknown statistic, or a level outside ``[0, 1]``.

    Examples:
        >>> scene = np.array([[[1.0, 3.0]], [[2.0, np.nan]]])  # (band, y, x)
        >>> # the NaN in band 1 invalidates that pixel in band 0 too
        >>> carrier_band_stats(scene, stats=("mean",))
        {'mean': array([1., 2.])}
        >>> out = carrier_band_stats(scene, stats=(), quantiles=(0.5,))
        >>> out["quantiles"].shape  # (len(quantiles), C)
        (1, 2)
        >>> float(carrier_band_stats(scene, per_band=False, stats=("max",))["max"])
        2.0
    """
    view = _pixel_view(x, dim, "carrier_band_stats")
    axis = view.band_axis if per_band else None
    out = dict(band_stats(view.data, view.valid, band_axis=axis, stats=stats))
    if quantiles:
        out["quantiles"] = band_quantiles(
            view.data, view.valid, band_axis=axis, q=quantiles
        )
    return out

docs.title: clahe(arr, *, window=None, clip_limit=0.01, nbins=256)
docs.text:
Apply contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization per image band.

The algorithm of :func:skimage.exposure.equalize_adapthist, written on the array namespace so it runs on NumPy and on JAX (under jax.jit too, one trace per shape) without scikit-image. Each (H, W) slice (every band of a (C, H, W) cube, every band of every frame of a (T, C, H, W) stack) is equalized independently:

  1. rescale to [0, 1] over its finite range, quantise to 14-bit grey levels and bin them into nbins;
  2. reflect-pad to whole tiles of window, take each tile's histogram, clip it at clip_limit times the tile size and redistribute the excess as scikit-image does;
  3. map each pixel through the cumulative histograms of its four nearest tiles, blended bilinearly, and map the result back to native units.

NaN pixels are excluded (filled with the slice median before the histograms, as before) and stay NaN. A constant or all-NaN slice is returned unchanged.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default arr Shaped[ndarray, '*dims']

Input array; trailing axes are (H, W).

required window int | tuple[int, int] | None

Contextual-region shape for the local histograms. None uses scikit-image's default (1/8 of the slice height / width).

None clip_limit float

Contrast-limiting clip threshold in [0, 1]. Default 0.01.

0.01 nbins int

Number of histogram bins. Default 256.

256

Returns:

Type Description Float[ndarray, '*dims']

Float array of the same shape, equalized per band.

Examples:

>>> ramp = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, 64).reshape(8, 8) ** 2
>>> out = clahe(ramp, window=4)
>>> out.shape, float(out.min()), float(out.max())
((8, 8), 0.0, 1.0)
>>> # a stack is equalized slice by slice
>>> clahe(np.stack([ramp, ramp]), window=4).shape
(2, 8, 8)
Source code in packages/geotoolz-ops/src/geoops/normalize/_src/array.py 
def clahe(
    arr: Shaped[np.ndarray, "*dims"],
    *,
    window: int | tuple[int, int] | None = None,
    clip_limit: float = 0.01,
    nbins: int = 256,
) -> Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"]:
    """Apply contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization per image band.

    The algorithm of :func:`skimage.exposure.equalize_adapthist`, written on
    the array namespace so it runs on NumPy and on JAX (under ``jax.jit`` too,
    one trace per shape) without scikit-image. Each ``(H, W)`` slice (every
    band of a ``(C, H, W)`` cube, every band of every frame of a
    ``(T, C, H, W)`` stack) is equalized independently:

    1. rescale to ``[0, 1]`` over its finite range, quantise to 14-bit grey
       levels and bin them into ``nbins``;
    2. reflect-pad to whole tiles of ``window``, take each tile's histogram,
       clip it at ``clip_limit`` times the tile size and redistribute the
       excess as scikit-image does;
    3. map each pixel through the cumulative histograms of its four nearest
       tiles, blended bilinearly, and map the result back to native units.

    NaN pixels are excluded (filled with the slice median before the
    histograms, as before) and stay NaN. A constant or all-NaN slice is
    returned unchanged.

    Args:
        arr: Input array; trailing axes are ``(H, W)``.
        window: Contextual-region shape for the local histograms.
            ``None`` uses scikit-image's default (1/8 of the slice height /
            width).
        clip_limit: Contrast-limiting clip threshold in ``[0, 1]``.
            Default ``0.01``.
        nbins: Number of histogram bins. Default ``256``.

    Returns:
        Float array of the same shape, equalized per band.

    Examples:
        >>> ramp = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, 64).reshape(8, 8) ** 2
        >>> out = clahe(ramp, window=4)
        >>> out.shape, float(out.min()), float(out.max())
        ((8, 8), 0.0, 1.0)
        >>> # a stack is equalized slice by slice
        >>> clahe(np.stack([ramp, ramp]), window=4).shape
        (2, 8, 8)
    """
    xp = namespace_of(arr)
    values = arr if arr.dtype == np.float64 else arr.astype(np.float64)
    shape = values.shape
    height, width = shape[-2:]
    kernel = _clahe_kernel(window, (height, width))
    v = xp.reshape(values, (-1, height, width))
    valid = xp.isfinite(v)
    vmin = xp.min(xp.where(valid, v, xp.inf), axis=(-2, -1), keepdims=True)
    vmax = xp.max(xp.where(valid, v, -xp.inf), axis=(-2, -1), keepdims=True)
    ok = vmax > vmin  # False for a constant or all-NaN slice
    span = xp.where(ok, vmax - vmin, 1.0)
    low = xp.where(ok, vmin, 0.0)
    median = xp.nanmedian(xp.where(ok & valid, v, xp.nan), axis=(-2, -1), keepdims=True)
    unit = xp.where(valid, (v - low) / span, (median - low) / span)
    unit = xp.where(ok, xp.clip(unit, 0.0, 1.0), 0.0)
    equalized = _equalize_adapthist(unit, kernel, clip_limit, nbins, xp)
    out = xp.where(valid & ok, equalized * span + low, v)
    return xp.reshape(out, shape)

docs.text:
Match source values to the empirical CDF of reference.

Per-band monotone remapping: each source value is replaced by the reference value at the same empirical quantile (reference_cdf then match_cdf). NaN pixels in the source are left untouched; NaNs in the reference are excluded from its CDF.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default source Float[ndarray, '*dims']

Array to remap. If 3-D+ ((C, H, W)), bands are matched independently.

required reference Float[ndarray, '*ref']

Reference array. Either band-matched (same leading band count as source) or a single 2-D map applied to every source band.

required

Returns:

Type Description Float[ndarray, '*dims']

Float array of the same shape as source with its per-band

Float[ndarray, '*dims']

histograms reshaped to the reference.

Example

histogram_match(np.array([[0.0, 1.0, 2.0]]), np.array([[10.0, 20.0, 30.0]])) array([[10., 20., 30.]])

Source code in packages/geotoolz-ops/src/geoops/normalize/_src/array.py 
def histogram_match(
    source: Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"],
    reference: Float[np.ndarray, "*ref"],
) -> Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"]:
    """Match source values to the empirical CDF of ``reference``.

    Per-band monotone remapping: each source value is replaced by the
    reference value at the same empirical quantile (`reference_cdf` then
    `match_cdf`). NaN pixels in the source are left untouched; NaNs in the
    reference are excluded from its CDF.

    Args:
        source: Array to remap. If 3-D+ (``(C, H, W)``), bands are
            matched independently.
        reference: Reference array. Either band-matched (same leading
            band count as ``source``) or a single 2-D map applied to
            every source band.

    Returns:
        Float array of the same shape as ``source`` with its per-band
        histograms reshaped to the reference.

    Example:
        >>> histogram_match(np.array([[0.0, 1.0, 2.0]]), np.array([[10.0, 20.0, 30.0]]))
        array([[10., 20., 30.]])
    """
    source = np.asarray(source, dtype=float)
    reference = np.asarray(reference, dtype=float)
    banded = source.ndim >= 3 and (
        reference.ndim == 2
        or (reference.ndim >= 3 and source.shape[0] == reference.shape[0])
    )
    n_bands = source.shape[0] if banded else 1
    flat = source.reshape(n_bands, -1)
    ref = reference.reshape(1 if reference.ndim == 2 or not banded else n_bands, -1)
    table = reference_cdf(ref, np.isfinite(ref))
    if table[0].shape[0] != n_bands:  # one 2-D map for every band
        table = tuple(np.repeat(t, n_bands, axis=0) for t in table)
    return match_cdf(flat, np.isfinite(flat), *table).reshape(source.shape)

def inverse_minmax_scale(
    arr: Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"],
    vmin: Float[np.ndarray, "*stat"] | float,
    vmax: Float[np.ndarray, "*stat"] | float,
    *,
    out_range: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 1.0),
    reduce_axes: tuple[int, ...] | None = (-2, -1),
) -> Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"]:
    r"""Undo :func:`minmax_scale`: map ``out_range`` back onto ``[vmin, vmax]``.

    .. math::

        x \;=\; \frac{y - o_{\min}}{o_{\max} - o_{\min}}
                \cdot (v_{\max} - v_{\min}) + v_{\min}

    Args:
        arr: Scaled float array. NaN pixels propagate through untouched.
        vmin: Scalar or per-band lower bound, as for `minmax_scale`.
        vmax: Scalar or per-band upper bound; ``vmax <= vmin`` reads the
            span as ``1``.
        out_range: The ``(out_min, out_max)`` range `minmax_scale` mapped
            into. Default ``(0.0, 1.0)``.
        reduce_axes: Axes the bounds were reduced over. Default
            ``(-2, -1)``; ``None`` for global bounds.

    Returns:
        Float array of the same shape as ``arr``.

    Raises:
        TypeError: ``arr`` is a georeader ``GeoTensor``.
        ValueError: If ``out_range`` is not a two-element increasing tuple.

    Examples:
        >>> x = np.array([[[1.0, 3.0]]])
        >>> inverse_minmax_scale(minmax_scale(x, 1.0, 3.0), 1.0, 3.0)
        array([[[1., 3.]]])
        >>> y = minmax_scale(x, 1.0, 3.0, out_range=(0.0, 255.0))
        >>> inverse_minmax_scale(y, 1.0, 3.0, out_range=(0.0, 255.0))
        array([[[1., 3.]]])
    """
    reject_geotensor(arr, "inverse_minmax_scale")
    out_min, out_max = validate_out_range(out_range)
    vmin_b = reshape_stat(vmin, arr, reduce_axes)
    vmax_b = reshape_stat(vmax, arr, reduce_axes)
    span = namespace_of(arr).where(vmax_b > vmin_b, vmax_b - vmin_b, 1.0)
    return (arr - out_min) / (out_max - out_min) * span + vmin_b

def inverse_robust_scale(
    arr: Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"],
    median: Float[np.ndarray, "*stat"] | float,
    iqr: Float[np.ndarray, "*stat"] | float,
    *,
    reduce_axes: tuple[int, ...] | None = (-2, -1),
) -> Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"]:
    r"""Undo :func:`robust_scale`.

    .. math::

        x \;=\; y \cdot (Q_{3} - Q_{1}) + \mathrm{median}

    Args:
        arr: Scaled float array. NaN pixels propagate through untouched.
        median: Scalar or per-band median, as for `robust_scale`.
        iqr: Scalar or per-band interquartile range; a zero ``iqr`` is
            read as ``1``.
        reduce_axes: Axes the statistics were reduced over. Default
            ``(-2, -1)``; ``None`` for global statistics.

    Returns:
        Float array of the same shape as ``arr``.

    Raises:
        TypeError: ``arr`` is a georeader ``GeoTensor``.

    Examples:
        >>> x = np.array([[[1.0, 3.0]]])
        >>> inverse_robust_scale(robust_scale(x, 2.0, 4.0), 2.0, 4.0)
        array([[[1., 3.]]])
        >>> # per-band statistics for a (C, H, W) cube
        >>> cube = np.ones((2, 1, 2))
        >>> inverse_robust_scale(cube, [0.0, 1.0], [2.0, 3.0])[:, 0, 0]
        array([2., 4.])
    """
    reject_geotensor(arr, "inverse_robust_scale")
    median_b = reshape_stat(median, arr, reduce_axes)
    iqr_b = reshape_stat(iqr, arr, reduce_axes)
    return arr * namespace_of(arr).where(iqr_b != 0, iqr_b, 1.0) + median_b

def inverse_standard_scale(
    arr: Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"],
    mean: Float[np.ndarray, "*stat"] | float,
    std: Float[np.ndarray, "*stat"] | float,
    *,
    reduce_axes: tuple[int, ...] | None = (-2, -1),
) -> Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"]:
    r"""Undo :func:`standard_scale`.

    .. math::

        x \;=\; y \cdot \sigma + \mu

    Args:
        arr: Scaled float array. NaN pixels propagate through untouched.
        mean: Scalar or per-band mean :math:`\mu`, as for `standard_scale`.
        std: Scalar or per-band standard deviation :math:`\sigma`; a zero
            ``std`` is read as ``1``, as `standard_scale` divides by it.
        reduce_axes: Axes the statistics were reduced over. Default
            ``(-2, -1)``; ``None`` for global statistics.

    Returns:
        Float array of the same shape as ``arr``.

    Raises:
        TypeError: ``arr`` is a georeader ``GeoTensor``.

    Examples:
        >>> x = np.array([[[1.0, 3.0]]])
        >>> inverse_standard_scale(standard_scale(x, 2.0, 0.5), 2.0, 0.5)
        array([[[1., 3.]]])
        >>> # a constant band (std 0) round-trips too
        >>> inverse_standard_scale(standard_scale(x, 1.0, 0.0), 1.0, 0.0)
        array([[[1., 3.]]])
    """
    reject_geotensor(arr, "inverse_standard_scale")
    mean_b = reshape_stat(mean, arr, reduce_axes)
    std_b = reshape_stat(std, arr, reduce_axes)
    return arr * namespace_of(arr).where(std_b != 0, std_b, 1.0) + mean_b

def log_scale(
    arr: Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"], *, base: float = 10.0, eps: float = 1e-6
) -> Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"]:
    r"""Apply log scaling with a small offset for zero-valued pixels.

    .. math::

        y \;=\; \log_{\text{base}}(\max(x, 0) + \epsilon)

    Compresses heavy-tailed distributions (radar backscatter, fire
    radiative power, ...). Negative inputs are clipped to zero before
    the log; ``eps`` keeps the log finite at zero.

    Args:
        arr: Input float array. NaN pixels propagate through untouched.
        base: Logarithm base. Must be positive and not equal to ``1``.
            Default ``10.0``.
        eps: Small positive offset added before the log. Default
            ``1e-6``.

    Returns:
        Float array of the same shape.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``base`` or ``eps`` is out of range.
    """

    xp = array_namespace(arr)
    return xp.log(xp.maximum(arr, 0.0) + eps) / math.log(base)

docs.title: match_cdf(x, valid, levels, values, ok)
docs.text:
Map each band of x through its CDF onto a reference_cdf table.

.. math::

y \;=\; G_c^{-1}\big(F_c(x)\big), \qquad
F_c(x) \;=\; \frac{\#\{\text{valid } x' \le x\}}{n_c}

:math:F_c comes from a sort and searchsorted (invalid values sort last as +inf), and :math:G_c^{-1} is a linear interpolation through the table, so this is exact rank matching with static shapes: it runs on NumPy and JAX, under jax.jit too (one trace per shape), and on a dask block holding whole bands.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x Float[ndarray, 'C N']

(C, N) float values, one band per row.

required valid Shaped[ndarray, 'C N']

(C, N) booleans; False leaves a value out of the CDF.

required levels Float[ndarray, 'C M']

(C, M) fractions from reference_cdf.

required values Float[ndarray, 'C M']

(C, M) values from reference_cdf.

required ok Shaped[ndarray, 'C 1']

(C, 1) from reference_cdf; a band whose reference has no valid value keeps x.

required

Returns:

Type Description Float[ndarray, 'C N']

(C, N) on x's backend; invalid entries keep x's value.

Example

table = reference_cdf(np.array([[10.0, 20.0, 30.0]]), None) x = np.array([[2.0, 0.0, 1.0]]) match_cdf(x, np.isfinite(x), *table) array([[30., 10., 20.]])

Source code in packages/geotoolz-ops/src/geoops/normalize/_src/array.py 
def match_cdf(
    x: Float[np.ndarray, "C N"],
    valid: Shaped[np.ndarray, "C N"],
    levels: Float[np.ndarray, "C M"],
    values: Float[np.ndarray, "C M"],
    ok: Shaped[np.ndarray, "C 1"],
) -> Float[np.ndarray, "C N"]:
    r"""Map each band of ``x`` through its CDF onto a `reference_cdf` table.

    .. math::

        y \;=\; G_c^{-1}\big(F_c(x)\big), \qquad
        F_c(x) \;=\; \frac{\#\{\text{valid } x' \le x\}}{n_c}

    :math:`F_c` comes from a sort and ``searchsorted`` (invalid values sort
    last as ``+inf``), and :math:`G_c^{-1}` is a linear interpolation through
    the table, so this is exact rank matching with static shapes: it runs on
    NumPy and JAX, under ``jax.jit`` too (one trace per shape), and on a
    dask block holding whole bands.

    Args:
        x: ``(C, N)`` float values, one band per row.
        valid: ``(C, N)`` booleans; ``False`` leaves a value out of the CDF.
        levels: ``(C, M)`` fractions from `reference_cdf`.
        values: ``(C, M)`` values from `reference_cdf`.
        ok: ``(C, 1)`` from `reference_cdf`; a band whose reference has no
            valid value keeps ``x``.

    Returns:
        ``(C, N)`` on ``x``'s backend; invalid entries keep ``x``'s value.

    Example:
        >>> table = reference_cdf(np.array([[10.0, 20.0, 30.0]]), None)
        >>> x = np.array([[2.0, 0.0, 1.0]])
        >>> match_cdf(x, np.isfinite(x), *table)
        array([[30., 10., 20.]])
    """
    xp = namespace_of(x)
    count = xp.sum(valid, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    ordered = xp.sort(xp.where(valid, x, xp.inf), axis=-1)
    rows = []
    for band in range(x.shape[0]):
        rank = xp.searchsorted(ordered[band], x[band], side="right")
        fraction = rank / xp.maximum(count[band], 1)
        rows.append(xp.interp(fraction, levels[band], values[band]))
    matched = xp.stack(rows)
    return xp.where(valid & (count > 0) & ok, matched, x)

Parameters:

required vmax Float[ndarray, '*stat'] | float

Scalar or per-band upper bound (maps to out_range[1]). Bands with vmax <= vmin fall back to a divisor of 1.

required out_range tuple[float, float]

(out_min, out_max) target range; must be increasing. Default (0.0, 1.0).

(0.0, 1.0) reduce_axes tuple[int, ...] | None

Axes the bounds were reduced over. Default (-2, -1); None for global bounds.

(-2, -1)

Returns:

Type Description Float[ndarray, '*dims']

Float array of the same shape as arr. Values outside

Float[ndarray, '*dims']

[vmin, vmax] are not clipped.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If out_range is not a two-element increasing tuple.

Source code in packages/geotoolz-ops/src/geoops/normalize/_src/array.py 
def minmax_scale(
    arr: Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"],
    vmin: Float[np.ndarray, "*stat"] | float,
    vmax: Float[np.ndarray, "*stat"] | float,
    *,
    out_range: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 1.0),
    reduce_axes: tuple[int, ...] | None = (-2, -1),
) -> Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"]:
    r"""Linearly map ``[vmin, vmax]`` into ``out_range``.

    .. math::

        y \;=\; \frac{x - v_{\min}}{v_{\max} - v_{\min}}
                \cdot (o_{\max} - o_{\min}) + o_{\min}

    Args:
        arr: Input float array. NaN pixels propagate through untouched.
        vmin: Scalar or per-band lower bound (maps to ``out_range[0]``).
        vmax: Scalar or per-band upper bound (maps to ``out_range[1]``).
            Bands with ``vmax <= vmin`` fall back to a divisor of ``1``.
        out_range: ``(out_min, out_max)`` target range; must be
            increasing. Default ``(0.0, 1.0)``.
        reduce_axes: Axes the bounds were reduced over. Default ``(-2, -1)``;
            ``None`` for global bounds.

    Returns:
        Float array of the same shape as ``arr``. Values outside
        ``[vmin, vmax]`` are *not* clipped.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``out_range`` is not a two-element increasing
            tuple.
    """
    out_min, out_max = validate_out_range(out_range)
    vmin_b = reshape_stat(vmin, arr, reduce_axes)
    vmax_b = reshape_stat(vmax, arr, reduce_axes)
    denom = namespace_of(arr).where(vmax_b > vmin_b, vmax_b - vmin_b, 1.0)
    return (arr - vmin_b) / denom * (out_max - out_min) + out_min

def per_band_stats(
    arr: Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"],
    *,
    percentiles: list[float] | tuple[float, ...] = (1.0, 99.0),
    reduce_axes: tuple[int, ...] | None = (-2, -1),
) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Compute NaN-aware statistics over spatial axes.

    Args:
        arr: Input float array, typically a channel-first ``(C, H, W)``
            cube. NaN pixels are excluded from every statistic.
        percentiles: Percentiles (in ``[0, 100]``) to compute alongside
            the moments. Default ``(1.0, 99.0)``.
        reduce_axes: Axes to reduce over. Default ``(-2, -1)`` yields one value
            per band; ``None`` reduces globally.

    Returns:
        Dict with keys ``"mean"``, ``"std"``, ``"min"``, ``"max"``
        (each shaped like the kept axes, e.g. ``(C,)``) and
        ``"percentiles"`` of shape ``(len(percentiles), C)``.
    """
    return {
        "mean": np.nanmean(arr, axis=reduce_axes),
        "std": np.nanstd(arr, axis=reduce_axes),
        "min": np.nanmin(arr, axis=reduce_axes),
        "max": np.nanmax(arr, axis=reduce_axes),
        "percentiles": np.nanpercentile(arr, percentiles, axis=reduce_axes),
    }

def power_scale(
    arr: Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"], *, gamma: float = 0.5
) -> Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"]:
    r"""Apply non-negative power scaling.

    .. math::

        y \;=\; \max(x, 0)^{\gamma}

    A simple gamma-style brightness curve; negative inputs are clipped
    to zero before the power to avoid complex results.

    Args:
        arr: Input float array. NaN pixels propagate through untouched.
        gamma: Power exponent. ``< 1`` brightens midtones, ``> 1``
            darkens. Must be strictly positive. Default ``0.5``.

    Returns:
        Float array of the same shape.

        ValueError: If ``gamma <= 0``.
    """
    check_positive("gamma", gamma)

docs.title: reference_cdf(reference, valid)
docs.text:
The per-band empirical CDF of reference, as a padded table for match_cdf.

For each band, the distinct valid values :math:v_1 < \dots < v_m and their cumulative fractions :math:G(v_k) = \#\{x \le v_k\} / n, the points that scikit-image's match_histograms interpolates through. Bands have different numbers of distinct values, so each row is padded to the longest with levels above 1 and its maximum, which an interpolation at a fraction in [0, 1] never reaches. Host NumPy only: a reference is concrete, and its table is a constant for match_cdf.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default reference Float[ndarray, 'C N']

(C, N) values, one band per row.

required valid Shaped[ndarray, 'C N']

(C, N) booleans; False leaves a value out.

required

Returns:

Type Description ``(levels, values, ok)``

(C, M) fractions, (C, M) values, and

Float[ndarray, 'C M']

(C, 1) whether the band has any valid value.

Example

levels, values, ok = reference_cdf(np.array([[1.0, 1.0, 3.0]]), None) levels.tolist(), values.tolist(), ok.tolist() ([[0.6666666666666666, 1.0]], [[1.0, 3.0]], [[True]])

Source code in packages/geotoolz-ops/src/geoops/normalize/_src/array.py 
def reference_cdf(
    reference: Float[np.ndarray, "C N"], valid: Shaped[np.ndarray, "C N"]
) -> tuple[
    Float[np.ndarray, "C M"], Float[np.ndarray, "C M"], Shaped[np.ndarray, "C 1"]
]:
    r"""The per-band empirical CDF of ``reference``, as a padded table for `match_cdf`.

    For each band, the distinct valid values :math:`v_1 < \dots < v_m` and
    their cumulative fractions :math:`G(v_k) = \#\{x \le v_k\} / n`, the
    points that scikit-image's ``match_histograms`` interpolates through.
    Bands have different numbers of distinct values, so each row is padded to
    the longest with levels above ``1`` and its maximum, which an
    interpolation at a fraction in ``[0, 1]`` never reaches. Host NumPy only:
    a reference is concrete, and its table is a constant for `match_cdf`.

    Args:
        reference: ``(C, N)`` values, one band per row.
        valid: ``(C, N)`` booleans; ``False`` leaves a value out.

    Returns:
        ``(levels, values, ok)``: ``(C, M)`` fractions, ``(C, M)`` values, and
        ``(C, 1)`` whether the band has any valid value.

    Example:
        >>> levels, values, ok = reference_cdf(np.array([[1.0, 1.0, 3.0]]), None)
        >>> levels.tolist(), values.tolist(), ok.tolist()
        ([[0.6666666666666666, 1.0]], [[1.0, 3.0]], [[True]])
    """
    reference = np.asarray(reference, dtype=float)
    if valid is None:
        valid = np.isfinite(reference)
    rows = []
    for band, keep in zip(reference, np.asarray(valid, dtype=bool), strict=True):
        values, counts = np.unique(band[keep], return_counts=True)
        rows.append((np.cumsum(counts) / max(int(keep.sum()), 1), values))
    width = max(1, *(values.size for _, values in rows))
    levels = np.empty((len(rows), width))
    table = np.empty((len(rows), width))
    for row, (fractions, values) in enumerate(rows):
        m = values.size
        levels[row, :m] = fractions
        levels[row, m:] = 2.0 + np.arange(width - m)
        table[row, :m] = values
        table[row, m:] = values[-1] if m else np.nan
    ok = np.array([[values.size > 0] for _, values in rows], dtype=bool)
    return levels, table, ok

def robust_scale(
    arr: Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"],
    median: Float[np.ndarray, "*stat"] | float,
    iqr: Float[np.ndarray, "*stat"] | float,
    *,
    reduce_axes: tuple[int, ...] | None = (-2, -1),
) -> Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"]:
    r"""Apply median/IQR scaling while preserving NaN pixels.

    .. math::

        y \;=\; \frac{x - \mathrm{median}}{Q_{3} - Q_{1}}

    The outlier-robust counterpart of :func:`standard_scale` — bright
    outliers (clouds, glint, saturation) barely move the median and
    interquartile range.

    Args:
        arr: Input float array. NaN pixels propagate through untouched.
        median: Scalar or per-band median (shape matching the kept
            axes).
        iqr: Scalar or per-band interquartile range ``Q3 - Q1``. Bands
            with ``iqr == 0`` fall back to a divisor of ``1``.
        reduce_axes: Axes the statistics were reduced over. Default
            ``(-2, -1)``; ``None`` for global statistics.

    Returns:
        Float array of the same shape as ``arr``.
    """
    median_b = reshape_stat(median, arr, reduce_axes)
    iqr_b = reshape_stat(iqr, arr, reduce_axes)
    denom = namespace_of(arr).where(iqr_b != 0, iqr_b, 1.0)
    return (arr - median_b) / denom

    arr: Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"],
    mean: Float[np.ndarray, "*stat"] | float,
    std: Float[np.ndarray, "*stat"] | float,
    *,
    reduce_axes: tuple[int, ...] | None = (-2, -1),
) -> Float[np.ndarray, "*dims"]:
    r"""Apply z-score scaling while preserving NaN pixels.

    .. math::

        y \;=\; \frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}

    Args:
        arr: Input float array. NaN pixels propagate through untouched.
        mean: Scalar or per-band mean :math:`\mu` (shape matching the
            kept axes, e.g. ``(C,)`` for a ``(C, H, W)`` input).
        std: Scalar or per-band standard deviation :math:`\sigma`. Bands
            with ``std == 0`` fall back to a divisor of ``1`` so a
            constant band maps to zero instead of ``inf`` / ``nan``.
        reduce_axes: Axes the statistics were reduced over. Default
            ``(-2, -1)``; ``None`` for global statistics.

        Float array of the same shape as ``arr``.

    std_b = reshape_stat(std, arr, reduce_axes)
    denom = namespace_of(arr).where(std_b != 0, std_b, 1.0)
    return (arr - mean_b) / denom

docs.title: Plume
docs.text:
Trace-gas retrieval post-processing for methane / CO₂ plumes — SBMP retrieval, detection masks, footprint vectorisation, integrated mass enhancement, and cross-sectional flux. Algorithm sources are cited in the operator docstrings (Varon et al., Frankenberg et al., Krings et al.).

  • Retrieval: SBMP (Sentinel-2 SWIR ratio, Varon 2021)
  • Detection / segmentation: PlumeMask, PlumeContours, PlumeFootprint (polygons from georeader.vectorize.get_polygons, measure.DEFAULT_REGIONPROPS metadata in pixel units)
  • Instance QA: PlumeShapeFilter (fiber-shape morphology gate), PlumeColumnStats (in-mask vs background statistics), PlumeQNDFeatures (quantile-normality-deviation features)
  • Quantification: ColumnToMass, IMEEstimate, CrossSectionalFlux, WindAdvectionCone
  • Tier-A primitives: plume_mask, convert_column_units, wind_advection_cone

Second carriers are positional call arguments on the primary carrier's pixel grid, never constructor kwargs (see Multi-input operators): IMEEstimate(wind_speed=3.5)(kg_m2, plume_mask), CrossSectionalFlux(...)(kg_m2, plume_mask), PlumeFootprint()(mask, kg_m2), SBMP()(scene, reference_scene), PlumeColumnStats()(labels, column), PlumeQNDFeatures()(labels, column, albedo).

class ColumnToMass(Operator):
    """Convert column enhancement units (ppm m / mol m^-2 / kg m^-2).

    Thin wrapper over :func:`convert_column_units`. The ppm m conversion
    assumes a standard molar volume (298.15 K, 1 atm); see that
    function's docstring for the exact relation and caveats. Nodata
    pixels (non-finite or equal to the fill value) are not converted:
    they hold ``NaN`` and the output declares ``fill_value=NaN``
    (a converted column is a new quantity, so the input's fill -- e.g.
    ``-9999`` ppm m -- is not carried over).

    Args:
        gas: ``"CH4"`` (default) or ``"CO2"``.
        units_in: Units of the input carrier.
        units_out: Desired output units.

    Examples:
        >>> kg_m2 = gz.plume.ColumnToMass(
        ...     gas="CH4", units_in="ppm_m", units_out="kg_m2",
        ... )(enhancement)
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy",)
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling()

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        gas: str = "CH4",
        units_in: ColumnUnit = "ppm_m",
        units_out: ColumnUnit = "kg_m2",
    ) -> None:
        self.gas = gas
        self.units_in = units_in
        self.units_out = units_out

    def _apply(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> GeoArray | np.ndarray:
        out = convert_column_units(
            np.asarray(gt),
            gas=self.gas,
            units_in=self.units_in,
            units_out=self.units_out,
        )
        if np.ndim(out) < 2:
            return wrap_like(gt, out)
        out = np.asarray(out, dtype=np.result_type(out, np.float32))
        return wrap_filled(gt, out, fill_value=np.nan)

Bases: Operator

Estimate cross-sectional flux at downwind transects.

For each transect at downwind distance :math:d_k, the operator integrates column mass across the plume:

.. math::

Q_k \;=\; U \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}
               \Omega(d_k, y) \, dy
    \;\approx\; U \sum_{i \in \mathrm{strip}_k}
               \Omega_i \,\Delta y_i

where :math:\mathrm{strip}_k is the set of plume pixels whose along-wind distance to the source falls within half a pixel of :math:d_k. This is the cross-section method of Krings et al. (2011) and Varon et al. (2018, appendix); a flat downwind profile of :math:Q_k versus :math:d_k confirms a steady-state estimate.

The enhancement carrier MUST be in kg/m^2 (see :class:ColumnToMass). Nodata enhancement pixels (non-finite or equal to the fill value) add nothing to a transect's flux. The implementation assumes (approximately) square pixels: it uses :math:\Delta y = \sqrt{\mathrm{pixel\_area}} as the across-wind pixel size. For strongly anisotropic pixel grids, reproject first.

Geo-dependent: transect placement and pixel size come from the carrier's transform and CRS, so the input must be a georeferenced GeoArray (plain arrays raise TypeError) in a projected CRS with metre units; a geographic CRS raises ValueError (reproject with :class:geoops.geom.Reproject first).

Called as op(enhancement, plume_mask): plume_mask is a boolean plume carrier on the enhancement's pixel grid (ValueError otherwise).

Northward wind component (m/s).

    source=(x0, y0),
    wind_u=3.0, wind_v=1.0,

class CrossSectionalFlux(Operator):
    r"""Estimate cross-sectional flux at downwind transects.

    For each transect at downwind distance :math:`d_k`, the operator
    integrates column mass across the plume:

    .. math::

        Q_k \;=\; U \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}
                       \Omega(d_k, y) \, dy
            \;\approx\; U \sum_{i \in \mathrm{strip}_k}
                       \Omega_i \,\Delta y_i

    where :math:`\mathrm{strip}_k` is the set of plume pixels whose
    along-wind distance to the source falls within half a pixel of
    :math:`d_k`. This is the cross-section method of Krings et al. (2011)
    and Varon et al. (2018, appendix); a flat downwind profile of
    :math:`Q_k` versus :math:`d_k` confirms a steady-state estimate.

    The enhancement carrier MUST be in kg/m^2 (see :class:`ColumnToMass`).
    Nodata enhancement pixels (non-finite or equal to the fill value) add
    nothing to a transect's flux.
    The implementation assumes (approximately) square pixels: it uses
    :math:`\Delta y = \sqrt{\mathrm{pixel\_area}}` as the across-wind
    pixel size. For strongly anisotropic pixel grids, reproject first.

    Geo-dependent: transect placement and pixel size come from the
    carrier's transform and CRS, so the input must be a georeferenced
    ``GeoArray`` (plain arrays raise ``TypeError``) in a projected CRS
    with metre units; a geographic CRS raises ``ValueError`` (reproject
    with :class:`geoops.geom.Reproject` first).

    Called as ``op(enhancement, plume_mask)``: ``plume_mask`` is a boolean
    plume carrier on the enhancement's pixel grid (``ValueError``
    otherwise).

    Args:
        source: ``(x, y)`` source coordinates in the carrier CRS (m).
        wind_u: Eastward wind component (m/s).
        wind_v: Northward wind component (m/s).
        n_transects: Number of downwind transects to evaluate.
        transect_spacing_m: Along-wind distance between transects (m).

    Returns:
        geopandas.GeoDataFrame: One row per transect: ``geometry``
            (across-wind ``LineString``), ``transect_id``,
            ``distance_m``, ``flux_kg_s``, ``n_pixels``.

    Examples:
        Evaluate fluxes at 100 m, 200 m, 300 m downwind::

            gdf = gz.plume.CrossSectionalFlux(
                source=(x0, y0),
                wind_u=3.0, wind_v=1.0,
                n_transects=3, transect_spacing_m=100.0,
            )(kg_m2, mask)
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy",)
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling(
        couples={"space"}, reach=None, kind="conversion"
    )

    _terminal: ClassVar[bool] = True

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        source: tuple[float, float],
        wind_u: float,
        wind_v: float,
        n_transects: int = 5,
        transect_spacing_m: float = 100.0,
    ) -> None:
        self.source = as_tuple(source)
        self.wind_u = wind_u
        self.wind_v = wind_v
        self.n_transects = n_transects
        self.transect_spacing_m = transect_spacing_m

    def _apply(
        self, gt: GeoArray, plume_mask: GeoArray | np.ndarray
    ) -> gpd.GeoDataFrame:
        LineString = optional_name(
            "shapely.geometry",
            "LineString",
            "vector",
            feature="geoops.plume.CrossSectionalFlux",
        )
        gpd = import_optional(
            "geopandas", "vector", feature="geoops.plume.CrossSectionalFlux"
        )
        require_ndim(gt, (2, 3), "CrossSectionalFlux")
        require_geoarray(gt, "CrossSectionalFlux")
        require_projected_crs(gt, "CrossSectionalFlux")
        require_grid_match(
            gt, plume_mask, "CrossSectionalFlux", names=("enhancement", "plume_mask")
        )
        wind_norm = float(np.hypot(self.wind_u, self.wind_v))
        if wind_norm == 0.0:
            raise ValueError("wind vector must be non-zero")
        mask = squeeze_single_band(
            np.asarray(plume_mask), name="CrossSectionalFlux"
        ).astype(bool)
        enhancement = _single_band_nan(gt, name="CrossSectionalFlux")
        area = pixel_area(affine_of(gt))
        width = float(np.sqrt(area))
        xs, ys = pixel_centers(mask.shape, affine_of(gt))
        dx = xs - self.source[0]
        dy = ys - self.source[1]
        along = (dx * self.wind_u + dy * self.wind_v) / wind_norm
        across = (-dx * self.wind_v + dy * self.wind_u) / wind_norm
        rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for idx in range(self.n_transects):
            distance = (idx + 1) * self.transect_spacing_m
            on_transect = mask & (np.abs(along - distance) <= width / 2.0)
            flux = float(np.nansum(enhancement[on_transect] * wind_norm * width))
            half_len = max(
                float(np.max(np.abs(across[mask]))) if mask.any() else width,
                width,
            )
            cx = self.source[0] + (self.wind_u / wind_norm) * distance
            cy = self.source[1] + (self.wind_v / wind_norm) * distance
            px = -self.wind_v / wind_norm
            py = self.wind_u / wind_norm
            line = LineString(
                [
                    (cx - px * half_len, cy - py * half_len),
                    (cx + px * half_len, cy + py * half_len),
                ]
            )
            rows.append(
                {
                    "geometry": line,
                    "transect_id": idx + 1,
                    "distance_m": float(distance),
                    "flux_kg_s": flux,
                    "n_pixels": int(on_transect.sum()),
                }
            )
        return gpd.GeoDataFrame(rows, geometry="geometry", crs=gt.crs)

Bases: Operator

Integrated Mass Enhancement (IME) flux estimator.

Implements the IME method of Varon et al. (2018), AMT Quantifying methane point sources from fine-scale satellite observations of atmospheric methane plumes:

.. math::

\mathrm{IME} \;=\; \sum_{i \in \mathrm{plume}}
                    \Omega_i \,\Delta A_i, \qquad
Q \;=\; \frac{U_{\mathrm{eff}}\,\mathrm{IME}}{L}

where :math:\Omega_i is the column enhancement (kg/m^2) of pixel :math:i, :math:\Delta A_i is its area (m^2), :math:L is the effective plume length (m) — see :func:plume_length — and :math:U_{\mathrm{eff}} is the effective wind speed (m/s). Varon et al. (2018) calibrate :math:U_{\mathrm{eff}} against LES simulations; this operator takes the calibrated value as wind_speed.

The enhancement carrier MUST be in kg/m^2. Use :class:ColumnToMass upstream to convert from ppm m or mol/m^2: passing other units silently produces nonsense. Nodata enhancement pixels (non-finite or equal to the fill value) add nothing to the IME.

Geo-dependent: pixel area (m^2) and plume length (m) are derived from the carrier's transform, so the input must be a georeferenced GeoArray (plain arrays raise TypeError) in a projected CRS with metre units; a geographic CRS raises ValueError (reproject with :class:geoops.geom.Reproject first).

Called as op(enhancement, plume_mask): plume_mask is a boolean carrier selecting plume pixels on the enhancement's pixel grid (same shape, transform and CRS; ValueError otherwise -- a mask on another grid would be indexed against the wrong pixels).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default wind_speed float

Effective wind speed :math:U_{\mathrm{eff}} in m/s.

required length_method Literal['max_axis', 'convex_hull', 'skeleton']

Length estimator: "max_axis", "convex_hull", or "skeleton". See :func:plume_length; "skeleton" raises ValueError for compact plumes whose skeleton collapses to a point.

'max_axis' pixel_area_m2 float | None

Override the pixel area (m^2); default is the absolute input transform determinant in the projected CRS's metres (exact on an equal-area projection; on UTM it ignores the projection's scale factor, a < 0.1 % error near the central meridian).

None return_uncertainty bool

Append emission_rate_uncertainty_kg_s.

True uncertainty_fraction float

Fractional 1-sigma uncertainty on Q. The default 0.5 follows Varon et al. (2018) Table 3.

0.5

Returns:

Type Description dict

Result with keys ime_kg, length_m, wind_speed_m_s, emission_rate_kg_s, and optionally emission_rate_uncertainty_kg_s.

Examples:

Estimate Q in kg/s from a ppm m enhancement map::

import geoops as gz

kg_m2 = gz.plume.ColumnToMass(units_in="ppm_m")(enhancement)
mask = gz.plume.PlumeMask(threshold="percentile:99")(kg_m2)
result = gz.plume.IMEEstimate(
    wind_speed=3.5,
    length_method="convex_hull",

    Implements the IME method of Varon et al. (2018), AMT
    *Quantifying methane point sources from fine-scale satellite
    observations of atmospheric methane plumes*:

    .. math::

        \mathrm{IME} \;=\; \sum_{i \in \mathrm{plume}}

    :math:`i`, :math:`\Delta A_i` is its area (m^2), :math:`L` is the
    effective plume length (m) — see :func:`plume_length` — and
    :math:`U_{\mathrm{eff}}` is the effective wind speed (m/s). Varon
    et al. (2018) calibrate :math:`U_{\mathrm{eff}}` against LES
    simulations; this operator takes the calibrated value as
    ``wind_speed``.

    The ``enhancement`` carrier MUST be in kg/m^2. Use
    :class:`ColumnToMass` upstream to convert from ppm m or mol/m^2:
    passing other units silently produces nonsense. Nodata enhancement
    pixels (non-finite or equal to the fill value) add nothing to the IME.

    Geo-dependent: pixel area (m^2) and plume length (m) are derived from
    the carrier's transform, so the input must be a georeferenced
    ``GeoArray`` (plain arrays raise ``TypeError``) in a projected CRS
    with metre units; a geographic CRS raises ``ValueError`` (reproject
    with :class:`geoops.geom.Reproject` first).

    Called as ``op(enhancement, plume_mask)``: ``plume_mask`` is a boolean
    carrier selecting plume pixels on the enhancement's pixel grid (same
    shape, transform and CRS; ``ValueError`` otherwise -- a mask on another
    grid would be indexed against the wrong pixels).

    Args:
        wind_speed: Effective wind speed :math:`U_{\mathrm{eff}}` in m/s.
        length_method: Length estimator: ``"max_axis"``, ``"convex_hull"``,
            or ``"skeleton"``. See :func:`plume_length`; ``"skeleton"``

            collapses to a point.

            absolute input transform determinant in the projected CRS's
            metres (exact on an equal-area projection; on UTM it ignores
            the projection's scale factor, a < 0.1 % error near the
            central meridian).
        return_uncertainty: Append ``emission_rate_uncertainty_kg_s``.
        uncertainty_fraction: Fractional 1-sigma uncertainty on Q. The
            default 0.5 follows Varon et al. (2018) Table 3.

    Returns:
        dict: Result with keys ``ime_kg``, ``length_m``,
            ``wind_speed_m_s``, ``emission_rate_kg_s``, and optionally
            ``emission_rate_uncertainty_kg_s``.

            result = gz.plume.IMEEstimate(
                wind_speed=3.5,

        *,
        wind_speed: float,
        length_method: Literal["max_axis", "convex_hull", "skeleton"] = "max_axis",
        pixel_area_m2: float | None = None,
        return_uncertainty: bool = True,
        uncertainty_fraction: float = 0.5,
    ) -> None:
        self.wind_speed = wind_speed
        self.length_method = length_method
        self.pixel_area_m2 = pixel_area_m2
        self.return_uncertainty = return_uncertainty
        if uncertainty_fraction < 0.0:
            raise ValueError("uncertainty_fraction must be non-negative")
        self.uncertainty_fraction = uncertainty_fraction

    def _apply(
        self, gt: GeoArray, plume_mask: GeoArray | np.ndarray
    ) -> dict[str, float]:
        require_ndim(gt, (2, 3), "IMEEstimate")
        require_geoarray(gt, "IMEEstimate")
        require_projected_crs(gt, "IMEEstimate")

            gt, plume_mask, "IMEEstimate", names=("enhancement", "plume_mask")
        )

            bool
        )
        enhancement = _single_band_nan(gt, name="IMEEstimate")

            self.pixel_area_m2
            if self.pixel_area_m2 is not None
            else pixel_area(affine_of(gt))
        )
        ime_kg = float(np.nansum(enhancement[mask] * area))
        length_m = plume_length(mask, affine_of(gt), method=self.length_method)
        rate = 0.0 if length_m == 0.0 else ime_kg * self.wind_speed / length_m
        out = {
            "ime_kg": ime_kg,
            "length_m": float(length_m),
            "wind_speed_m_s": float(self.wind_speed),
            "emission_rate_kg_s": float(rate),
        }
        if self.return_uncertainty:
            out["emission_rate_uncertainty_kg_s"] = float(
                abs(rate) * self.uncertainty_fraction
            )
        return out

Bases: Operator

Per-instance in-mask vs background statistics of a column field.

Adapted from Pérez Carrasco et al. (2026), rfc_utils.xch4_metrics. For every non-zero label in the input map, returns a row with the in-mask mean, the out-of-mask (background) mean / std, and three derived metrics used by the paper's Random-Forest false-plume classifier:

  • contrast = mean_plume / mean_background
  • z_score = (mean_plume - mean_background) / std_background
  • intensity_per_area = (sum_plume - mean_background * n_plume) / n_plume

Nodata column pixels (non-finite or equal to the column carrier's fill value) are left out of every statistic.

Called as op(labels, column): column is the column field (single-band GeoArray or plain array) on the label map's pixel grid (ValueError otherwise).

class PlumeColumnStats(Operator):
    """Per-instance in-mask vs background statistics of a column field.

    Adapted from Pérez Carrasco et al. (2026), ``rfc_utils.xch4_metrics``.
    For every non-zero label in the input map, returns a row with the
    in-mask mean, the out-of-mask (background) mean / std, and three
    derived metrics used by the paper's Random-Forest false-plume
    classifier:

    - ``contrast`` = ``mean_plume / mean_background``
    - ``z_score`` = ``(mean_plume - mean_background) / std_background``
    - ``intensity_per_area`` = ``(sum_plume - mean_background * n_plume)
      / n_plume``

    Nodata column pixels (non-finite or equal to the column carrier's
    fill value) are left out of every statistic.

    Called as ``op(labels, column)``: ``column`` is the column field
    (single-band ``GeoArray`` or plain array) on the label map's pixel
    grid (``ValueError`` otherwise).
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy",)
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling(
        couples={"space"}, reach=None, kind="conversion"
    )

    _terminal: ClassVar[bool] = True

    def _apply(
        self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray, column: GeoArray | np.ndarray
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        reject_geotensor(gt, "PlumeColumnStats")
        require_ndim(gt, (2, 3), "PlumeColumnStats")
        require_grid_match(gt, column, "PlumeColumnStats", names=("labels", "column"))
        labels = squeeze_single_band(np.asarray(gt), name="PlumeColumnStats").astype(
            np.int64, copy=False
        )
        col_arr = _single_band_nan(column, name="PlumeColumnStats").astype(
            float, copy=False
        )
        if col_arr.shape != labels.shape:
            raise ValueError(
                "column shape "
                f"{col_arr.shape} does not match label shape {labels.shape}"
            )
        rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for lbl, compact, bbox in _iter_instances(labels):
            y0, x0, y1, x1 = bbox
            full_mask = np.zeros_like(col_arr, dtype=bool)
            full_mask[y0:y1, x0:x1] = compact
            mean_plume, bg_mean, bg_std, contrast, z_score, ipa = _in_out_mask_stats(
                col_arr, full_mask
            )
            rows.append(
                {
                    "label": lbl,
                    "area": int(compact.sum()),
                    "mean_enhancement": mean_plume,
                    "background_mean": bg_mean,
                    "background_std": bg_std,
                    "contrast": contrast,
                    "z_score": z_score,
                    "intensity_per_area": ipa,
                }
            )
        if not rows:
            return pd.DataFrame(
                columns=[
                    "label",
                    "area",
                    "mean_enhancement",
                    "background_mean",
                    "background_std",
                    "contrast",
                    "z_score",
                    "intensity_per_area",
                ]
            )
        return pd.DataFrame(rows)

Bases: Operator

Connected-component labelling of a plume mask.

Returns either an int32 label image (default) or a boolean mask of the retained components. Component size threshold and connectivity follow :func:label_components.

Nodata pixels (non-finite -- e.g. a NaN score -- or equal to the input's fill value) are never part of a contour. In the boolean output they are False (fill_value=False). In the label image they hold the input's fill value when it is a non-positive int32 value (e.g. -9999, so it cannot collide with a label); otherwise (NaN, no fill, or a positive fill) they are 0 (background), and a GeoArray output then carries fill_value=0.

Examples:

>>> labels = gz.plume.PlumeContours(min_area_px=50)(mask)

class PlumeContours(Operator):
    """Connected-component labelling of a plume mask.

    Returns either an int32 label image (default) or a boolean mask of
    the retained components. Component size threshold and connectivity
    follow :func:`label_components`.

    Nodata pixels (non-finite -- e.g. a ``NaN`` score -- or equal to the
    input's fill value) are never part of a contour. In the boolean
    output they are ``False`` (``fill_value=False``). In the
    label image they hold the input's fill value when it is a
    non-positive int32 value (e.g. ``-9999``, so it cannot collide with
    a label); otherwise (``NaN``, no fill, or a
    positive fill) they are ``0`` (background), and a GeoArray output
    then carries ``fill_value=0``.

    Examples:
        >>> labels = gz.plume.PlumeContours(min_area_px=50)(mask)
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy",)
    # connected components
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling(couples={"space"}, reach=None)

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        min_area_px: int = 50,
        return_labels: bool = True,
        connectivity: Connectivity = 8,
    ) -> None:
        self.min_area_px = min_area_px
        self.return_labels = return_labels
        self.connectivity = connectivity

    @over_frames
    def _apply(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> GeoArray | np.ndarray:
        valid = valid_pixels(gt)
        labels = label_components(
            squeeze_single_band(np.asarray(gt), name="PlumeContours").astype(bool)
            & valid,
            min_area_px=self.min_area_px,
            connectivity=self.connectivity,
        )
        if not self.return_labels:
            return wrap_like(gt, labels > 0, fill_value=False)
        # ``carried_fill`` is None unless the fill is an int32 value; a
        # positive fill would collide with a component label.
        fill = carried_fill(gt, labels.dtype)
        if fill is None or isinstance(fill, bool | np.bool_) or fill > 0:
            fill = 0
        return wrap_filled(gt, labels, fill_value=fill, valid=valid)

Bases: Operator

Vectorize a plume mask into polygons with per-plume metadata.

The region properties come from the same machinery as :class:geoops.measure.RegionProps (defaults to :data:geoops.measure.DEFAULT_REGIONPROPS, pixel units) and the polygons from :func:georeader.vectorize.get_polygons. Returns a GeoDataFrame with one row per surviving plume: geometry, area_m2, centroid, mean_enhancement / max_enhancement (if enhancement is supplied), n_pixels, label_id, and skimage region properties such as major_axis_length, orientation, eccentricity, solidity, perimeter, bbox-*, and inertia_tensor_eigvals-*.

class PlumeFootprint(Operator):
    """Vectorize a plume mask into polygons with per-plume metadata.

    The region properties come from the same machinery as
    :class:`geoops.measure.RegionProps` (defaults to
    :data:`geoops.measure.DEFAULT_REGIONPROPS`, pixel units) and the
    polygons from :func:`georeader.vectorize.get_polygons`. Returns a
    ``GeoDataFrame`` with one row per surviving plume: ``geometry``, ``area_m2``,
    ``centroid``,
    ``mean_enhancement`` / ``max_enhancement`` (if ``enhancement`` is
    supplied), ``n_pixels``, ``label_id``, and skimage region properties such as
    ``major_axis_length``, ``orientation``, ``eccentricity``, ``solidity``,
    ``perimeter``, ``bbox-*``, and ``inertia_tensor_eigvals-*``.

    Nodata pixels of a boolean mask never form a polygon, non-positive
    labels are background, and nodata ``enhancement`` pixels are ignored
    by the per-polygon statistics.

    Geo-dependent: polygonisation needs the carrier's transform and CRS,
    so the input must be a georeferenced ``GeoArray`` (plain arrays
    raise ``TypeError``). Areas are in m^2 and the simplify tolerance in
    m, so the CRS must be projected with metre units; a geographic CRS
    raises ``ValueError`` (reproject with :class:`geoops.geom.Reproject`
    first).

    Args:
        min_area_m2: Drop polygons smaller than this area (m^2).
        simplify_tolerance: Douglas-Peucker tolerance (m) for polygon
            simplification; ``None`` to skip.
        properties: Region properties forwarded to ``regionprops_table``.
        extra_properties: User-defined ``regionprops_table`` callables.

    Called as ``op(mask, enhancement=None)``. The optional ``enhancement``
    carrier must sit on the mask's pixel grid (``ValueError`` otherwise);
    it enables the ``mean_enhancement`` / ``max_enhancement`` statistics
    per polygon.

    Examples:
        >>> gdf = gz.plume.PlumeFootprint(min_area_m2=500.0)(mask, kg_m2)
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy",)
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling(
        couples={"space"}, reach=None, kind="conversion"
    )

    _terminal: ClassVar[bool] = True

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        min_area_m2: float = 500.0,
        simplify_tolerance: float | None = 15.0,
        properties: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        extra_properties: Sequence[Callable[..., Any]] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.min_area_m2 = min_area_m2
        self.simplify_tolerance = simplify_tolerance
        self.properties = tuple(
            DEFAULT_REGIONPROPS if properties is None else properties
        )
        self.extra_properties = (
            None
            if extra_properties is None
            else tuple(
                reject_config_summary(f, "extra_properties") for f in extra_properties
            )
        )

    def _apply(
        self, gt: GeoArray, enhancement: GeoArray | np.ndarray | None = None
    ) -> gpd.GeoDataFrame:
        gpd = import_optional(
            "geopandas", "vector", feature="geoops.plume.PlumeFootprint"
        )
        unary_union = optional_name(
            "shapely.ops",
            "unary_union",
            "vector",
            feature="geoops.plume.PlumeFootprint",
        )
        vectorize = optional_name(
            "georeader",
            "vectorize",
            "sensors",
            feature="geoops.plume.PlumeFootprint",
        )
        require_ndim(gt, (2, 3), "PlumeFootprint")
        require_geoarray(gt, "PlumeFootprint")
        require_projected_crs(gt, "PlumeFootprint")
        if enhancement is not None:
            require_grid_match(
                gt, enhancement, "PlumeFootprint", names=("mask", "enhancement")
            )
        mask_arr = squeeze_single_band(np.asarray(gt), name="PlumeFootprint")
        if mask_arr.dtype == bool:
            labels = label_components(
                mask_arr & squeeze_single_band(valid_pixels(gt), name="PlumeFootprint"),
                min_area_px=1,
                connectivity=8,
            )
        else:
            # Non-positive labels (background, or a label image's fill
            # value such as -9999) are not plumes.
            labels = np.where(mask_arr > 0, mask_arr, 0).astype(np.int32, copy=False)
        enh = (
            None
            if enhancement is None
            else _single_band_nan(enhancement, name="PlumeFootprint")
        )
        properties = list(self.properties)
        if enh is not None:
            properties.extend(
                prop
                for prop in ("centroid_weighted", "mean_intensity", "max_intensity")
                if prop not in properties
            )
        props = regionprops_frame(
            labels,
            intensity_image=enh,
            properties=properties,
            extra_properties=self.extra_properties,
        )
        # Cast keys to int defensively: skimage returns numpy-int labels and
        # pandas to_dict("index") propagates that dtype. Python int hashes
        # equal in CPython but the explicit cast makes the lookup contract
        # obvious and survives dtype changes upstream.
        #
        # When the caller's ``properties`` omits ``"label"`` we still need a
        # per-component lookup, so synthesise it from ``regionprops_table``'s
        # row order (which mirrors ``sorted(unique(labels) - {0})``).
        if props.empty:
            props_by_label = {}
        else:
            if "label" in props.columns:
                indexed = props.set_index("label", drop=False)
            else:
                synthetic_labels = sorted(int(v) for v in np.unique(labels) if v != 0)
                indexed = props.copy()
                indexed.index = pd.Index(synthetic_labels[: len(indexed)])
            props_by_label = {int(k): v for k, v in indexed.to_dict("index").items()}

        rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for label_id in sorted(int(v) for v in np.unique(labels) if v != 0):
            component = labels == label_id
            n_pixels = int(component.sum())
            # One component can still vectorise to several 4-connected
            # polygons (diagonal-only contacts); union them.
            geometries = vectorize.get_polygons(
                component, min_area=0.0, tolerance=0.0, transform=affine_of(gt)
            )
            if not geometries:
                continue
            geometry = unary_union(geometries)
            if self.simplify_tolerance is not None:
                geometry = geometry.simplify(
                    self.simplify_tolerance, preserve_topology=True
                )
            area_m2 = float(geometry.area)
            if area_m2 < self.min_area_m2:
                continue
            component_values = None if enh is None else enh[component]
            region_props = props_by_label.get(label_id, {})

            # Bind region_props / component_values via default args to avoid
            # the late-binding closure trap that ruff B023 flags.
            def _nan_safe(
                reducer: Callable[[np.ndarray], float],
                key: str,
                rp: dict[str, Any] = region_props,
                vals: np.ndarray | None = component_values,
            ) -> float:
                # Prefer the regionprops_table value, but fall back to the
                # NaN-aware reducer when skimage propagates NaN through
                # ``mean_intensity`` / ``max_intensity`` (it does not ignore
                # NaNs internally). ``vals`` is non-None here.
                rp_val = rp.get(key)
                if rp_val is None or not np.isfinite(float(rp_val)):
                    return float(reducer(vals))
                return float(rp_val)

            mean_enhancement = (
                None
                if component_values is None
                else _nan_safe(np.nanmean, "mean_intensity")
            )
            max_enhancement = (
                None
                if component_values is None
                else _nan_safe(np.nanmax, "max_intensity")
            )
            rows.append(
                {
                    **region_props,
                    "geometry": geometry,
                    "area_m2": area_m2,
                    "centroid": geometry.centroid,
                    "mean_enhancement": mean_enhancement,
                    "max_enhancement": max_enhancement,
                    "n_pixels": n_pixels,
                    "label_id": label_id,
                }
            )
        if not rows:
            # No surviving components (empty mask, or all polygons filtered
            # out by ``min_area_m2``). Construct an empty GeoDataFrame with
            # the expected schema so downstream consumers see a stable
            # column layout instead of a constructor error.
            return gpd.GeoDataFrame(
                {
                    "geometry": [],
                    "area_m2": [],
                    "centroid": [],
                    "mean_enhancement": [],
                    "max_enhancement": [],
                    "n_pixels": [],
                    "label_id": [],
                },
                geometry="geometry",
                crs=gt.crs,
            )
        return gpd.GeoDataFrame(rows, geometry="geometry", crs=gt.crs)

    def get_config(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "min_area_m2": self.min_area_m2,
            "simplify_tolerance": self.simplify_tolerance,
            "properties": list(self.properties),
            "extra_properties": None
            if self.extra_properties is None
            else [{"callable": callable_name(f)} for f in self.extra_properties],
        }

class PlumeMask(Operator):
    """Binary plume mask from a single-band score or enhancement map.

    Thresholds the input (absolute number, Otsu, or percentile) and
    drops connected components smaller than ``min_area_px`` pixels — the
    Frankenberg et al. (2016) detection convention, also used by Varon
    et al. (2018, 2021) for S2/AVIRIS plume identification.

    Args:
        threshold: ``float`` (absolute), ``"otsu"``, or
            ``"percentile:<p>"`` with ``p`` in [0, 100].
        min_area_px: Minimum component size in pixels.
        connectivity: 4 or 8 connectivity for component labelling.
        nbins: Histogram bins for the ``"otsu"`` threshold (see
            :func:`geoops.segment.otsu_threshold`); ignored by the other modes.
            Default ``256``.

    Nodata pixels (non-finite or equal to the input's fill value) are
    excluded from the Otsu / percentile threshold and are always
    ``False`` in the mask, which declares ``fill_value=False``.

    Examples:
        >>> mask = gz.plume.PlumeMask(
        ...     threshold="percentile:99.5", min_area_px=50,
        ... )(enhancement)
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy",)
    # a scene threshold, then connected components
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling(couples={"space"}, reach=None)

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        threshold: ThresholdMode = "otsu",
        min_area_px: int = 50,
        connectivity: Connectivity = 8,
        nbins: int = 256,
    ) -> None:
        self.threshold = threshold
        self.min_area_px = min_area_px
        self.connectivity = connectivity
        self.nbins = nbins

    @over_frames
    def _apply(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> GeoArray | np.ndarray:
        mask = plume_mask(
            _single_band_nan(gt, name="PlumeMask"),
            threshold=self.threshold,
            min_area_px=self.min_area_px,
            connectivity=self.connectivity,
            nbins=self.nbins,
        )
        return wrap_like(gt, mask, fill_value=False)

class PlumeQNDFeatures(Operator):
    """Per-instance Quantile-Normality-Deviation features for plume QA.

    Adapted from Pérez Carrasco et al. (2026) — the feature pipeline that
    feeds the Random-Forest false-plume classifier
    (``rfc_utils.get_QND_df_cms`` / ``get_plume_info``). For each non-zero
    label in the input map this operator emits one row containing:

    - ``qnd_column_*`` — polynomial coefficients of the
      Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance between the in-mask CDF of the column
      field and a Gaussian fit to the full scene's column distribution,
      sampled across 100 percentiles in ``[0.01, 0.99]``.
    - ``qnd_albedo_*`` — same construction over the optional albedo field.
    - ``n_clumps`` — DBSCAN cluster count of in-mask pixels above the
      ``perc_threshold`` percentile (per the paper's clump-count signal).
    - ``contrast`` / ``z_score`` / ``intensity_per_area`` — the same stats
      that :class:`PlumeColumnStats` emits, included so a single call
      assembles the full feature vector used by the paper.

    Nodata column / albedo pixels (non-finite or equal to the carrier's
    fill value) are left out of every feature.

    Called as ``op(labels, column, albedo=None)``: ``column`` is the
    column-enhancement carrier and ``albedo`` an optional albedo carrier,
    both on the label map's pixel grid (``ValueError`` otherwise). Without
    ``albedo`` the ``qnd_albedo_*`` coefficients are NaN.

    Args:
        degree: Degree of the QND polynomial (paper default: 6).
        eps: DBSCAN ``eps`` (pixels).
        min_samples: DBSCAN ``min_samples``.
        perc_threshold: Percentile (within the instance mask) above which
            pixels are eligible for clustering.
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy",)
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling(
        couples={"space"}, reach=None, kind="conversion"
    )

    _terminal: ClassVar[bool] = True

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        degree: int = 6,
        eps: float = 50.0,
        min_samples: int = 50,
        perc_threshold: float = 98.0,
    ) -> None:
        if degree < 1:
            raise ValueError("degree must be >= 1")
        if eps <= 0:
            raise ValueError("eps must be positive")
        if min_samples < 1:
            raise ValueError("min_samples must be >= 1")
        if not 0.0 < perc_threshold < 100.0:
            raise ValueError("perc_threshold must be in (0, 100)")
        self.degree = int(degree)
        self.eps = float(eps)
        self.min_samples = int(min_samples)
        self.perc_threshold = float(perc_threshold)

    def _apply(
        self,
        gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray,
        column: GeoArray | np.ndarray,
        albedo: GeoArray | np.ndarray | None = None,
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        reject_geotensor(gt, "PlumeQNDFeatures")
        require_ndim(gt, (2, 3), "PlumeQNDFeatures")
        require_grid_match(gt, column, "PlumeQNDFeatures", names=("labels", "column"))
        if albedo is not None:
            require_grid_match(
                gt, albedo, "PlumeQNDFeatures", names=("labels", "albedo")
            )
        labels = squeeze_single_band(np.asarray(gt), name="PlumeQNDFeatures").astype(
            np.int64, copy=False
        )
        col_arr = _single_band_nan(column, name="PlumeQNDFeatures").astype(
            float, copy=False
        )
        if col_arr.shape != labels.shape:
            raise ValueError(
                "column shape "
                f"{col_arr.shape} does not match label shape {labels.shape}"
            )
        if albedo is None:
            alb_arr = None
        else:
            alb_arr = _single_band_nan(albedo, name="PlumeQNDFeatures").astype(
                float, copy=False
            )
            if alb_arr.shape != labels.shape:
                raise ValueError(
                    "albedo shape "
                    f"{alb_arr.shape} does not match label shape {labels.shape}"
                )

        col_keys = [f"qnd_column_c{i}" for i in range(self.degree + 1)]
        alb_keys = [f"qnd_albedo_c{i}" for i in range(self.degree + 1)]
        rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for lbl, compact, bbox in _iter_instances(labels):
            y0, x0, y1, x1 = bbox
            full_mask = np.zeros_like(col_arr, dtype=bool)
            full_mask[y0:y1, x0:x1] = compact
            qnd_col = _qnd_polynomial(col_arr, full_mask, self.degree)
            qnd_alb = (
                _qnd_polynomial(alb_arr, full_mask, self.degree)
                if alb_arr is not None
                else np.full(self.degree + 1, np.nan)
            )
            n_clumps = _dbscan_clump_count(
                col_arr,
                full_mask,
                eps=self.eps,
                min_samples=self.min_samples,
                perc_threshold=self.perc_threshold,
            )
            _mp, _bm, _bs, contrast, z_score, ipa = _in_out_mask_stats(
                col_arr, full_mask
            )
            row: dict[str, Any] = {
                "label": lbl,
                "area": int(compact.sum()),
                "n_clumps": n_clumps,
                "contrast": contrast,
                "z_score": z_score,
                "intensity_per_area": ipa,
            }
            row.update(dict(zip(col_keys, qnd_col.tolist(), strict=True)))
            row.update(dict(zip(alb_keys, qnd_alb.tolist(), strict=True)))
            rows.append(row)

        if not rows:
            empty_cols = [
                "label",
                "area",
                "n_clumps",
                "contrast",
                "z_score",
                "intensity_per_area",
                *col_keys,
                *alb_keys,
            ]
            return pd.DataFrame(columns=empty_cols)
        return pd.DataFrame(rows)

  4. fiber_width = area / fiber_length.
  5. Keep iff min_fiber_to_major_ratio <= fiber_length / major_axis <= max_fiber_to_major_ratio AND min_fiber_width <= fiber_width <= max_fiber_width.

Surviving instances keep their original integer labels; rejected instances are mapped to background (0).

class PlumeShapeFilter(Operator):
    """Drop instance labels that fail a fiber-shape morphology gate.

    Adapted from Pérez Carrasco et al. (2026), ``physical_constraints.
    apply_physical_constraints`` — a post-Mask R-CNN gate that distinguishes
    elongated plume features from compact false positives. Per instance:

    1. ``area = mask.sum()``; drop when below ``min_area_px``.
    2. ``fiber_length`` = longest Euclidean path through the skeleton, in
       pixel widths (diagonal steps count ``sqrt(2)``; see
       :func:`geoops.measure.skeleton_length`).
    3. ``major_axis`` = ``regionprops.axis_major_length`` — the PCA-based
       major axis of the equivalent ellipse. The original paper uses
       ``cv2.minAreaRect`` (rotated minimum-area rectangle), avoided here
       to keep the optional-dependency surface unchanged; the two measures
       agree closely for typical plume morphologies.
    4. ``fiber_width = area / fiber_length``.
    5. Keep iff
       ``min_fiber_to_major_ratio <= fiber_length / major_axis
       <= max_fiber_to_major_ratio`` AND
       ``min_fiber_width <= fiber_width <= max_fiber_width``.

    Surviving instances keep their original integer labels; rejected
    instances are mapped to background (``0``).

    Args:
        min_area_px: Minimum pixel count to consider an instance.
        min_fiber_to_major_ratio: Lower bound on ``fiber/major``.
        max_fiber_to_major_ratio: Upper bound on ``fiber/major``.
        min_fiber_width: Lower bound on ``area / fiber_length``.
        max_fiber_width: Upper bound on ``area / fiber_length``.
    """

    backends: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("numpy",)
    # shape measures of connected components
    coupling: ClassVar[Coupling] = Coupling(couples={"space"}, reach=None)

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        min_area_px: int = 50,
        min_fiber_to_major_ratio: float = 1.0,
        max_fiber_to_major_ratio: float = 10.0,
        min_fiber_width: float = 1.0,
        max_fiber_width: float = 100.0,
    ) -> None:
        if min_area_px < 0:
            raise ValueError("min_area_px must be non-negative")
        if min_fiber_to_major_ratio < 0 or max_fiber_to_major_ratio <= 0:
            raise ValueError("fiber-to-major ratio bounds must be non-negative")
        if min_fiber_to_major_ratio > max_fiber_to_major_ratio:
            raise ValueError("min_fiber_to_major_ratio must be <= max")
        if min_fiber_width < 0 or max_fiber_width <= 0:
            raise ValueError("fiber width bounds must be non-negative")
        if min_fiber_width > max_fiber_width:
            raise ValueError("min_fiber_width must be <= max")
        self.min_area_px = int(min_area_px)
        self.min_fiber_to_major_ratio = float(min_fiber_to_major_ratio)
        self.max_fiber_to_major_ratio = float(max_fiber_to_major_ratio)
        self.min_fiber_width = float(min_fiber_width)
        self.max_fiber_width = float(max_fiber_width)

    @over_frames
    def _apply(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> GeoArray | np.ndarray:
        labels = squeeze_single_band(np.asarray(gt), name="PlumeShapeFilter").astype(
            np.int64, copy=False
        )
        kept: set[int] = set()
        for lbl, compact, _bbox in _iter_instances(labels):
            area = int(compact.sum())
            if area < self.min_area_px:
                continue
            fiber_length = skeleton_length(compact)
            if fiber_length <= 0:
                continue
            major_axis = _major_axis_length(compact)
            if major_axis <= 0:
                continue
            ratio = fiber_length / major_axis
            fiber_width = area / fiber_length
            if not (
                self.min_fiber_to_major_ratio <= ratio <= self.max_fiber_to_major_ratio
            ):
                continue
            if not self.min_fiber_width <= fiber_width <= self.max_fiber_width:
                continue
            kept.add(lbl)

        if not kept:
            out = np.zeros_like(labels, dtype=np.int32)
        else:
            keep_mask = np.isin(labels, list(kept))
            out = np.where(keep_mask, labels, 0).astype(np.int32, copy=False)
        return wrap_like(gt, out, fill_value=0)

docs.text:
Bases: Operator

Single-band multi-pass Sentinel-2 SWIR ratio retrieval.

Emits a unitless methane "enhancement score" that highlights pixels where SWIR-2 (B12, ~2200 nm — a strong CH4 absorption window) is depressed relative to SWIR-1 (B11, ~1600 nm — weakly absorbing).

With a second positional carrier, the reference_scene (a clean-air acquisition over the same geography and pixel grid), the operator computes the log-ratio change

.. math::

\Delta \;=\; \log\!\Bigl(\tfrac{\rho_{B11} + \varepsilon}
                               {\rho_{B12} + \varepsilon}\Bigr)
           - \log\!\Bigl(\tfrac{\rho^{ref}_{B11} + \varepsilon}
                               {\rho^{ref}_{B12} + \varepsilon}\Bigr)

following Varon et al. (2021) — Satellite discovery of anomalously large methane point sources from oil/gas production (RSE, 251). The reference-scene formulation cancels static surface signatures so plume pixels dominate :math:\Delta.

Without a reference scene the operator falls back to the same-scene normalized SWIR contrast (SWIR1 - SWIR2) / (SWIR1 + SWIR2 + eps), which is a cheap detection prefilter (Ehret et al., 2022, TGRS) but is not a quantitative column retrieval — pair it with ColumnToMass only when calibrated against a per-scene ppm m mapping.

Inputs are radiance or reflectance arrays with band axis axis; negative values are clipped to zero before the log to keep the operator finite over noisy radiances. The output is single-band; nodata pixels (non-finite or equal to the fill value in any band of the input or the reference scene) hold NaN, and a GeoArray output declares fill_value=NaN.

Band names are resolved with the package-wide resolver (:func:geoops._src.bands.resolve_band: attrs band_names, then descriptions, then bands), so a GeoArray must name its bands. Only a plain ndarray with exactly 12 bands falls back to the Sentinel-2 L2A order (B1-B8, B8A, B9, B11, B12; no B10); on any other unnamed input pass integer indices.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default swir1 BandRef

Index or band name of the SWIR-1 channel. Default "B11".

'B11' swir2 BandRef

Index or band name of the SWIR-2 channel. Default "B12".

'B12' dim str

Name of the band dim (default "band"); its position is read from the carrier's dims.

'band' axis int | None

Deprecated: the band axis position. -3 maps to dim="band"; removed in the next minor release.

None eps float

Numerical guard against division by zero. Default 1e-10.

1e-10

Called as op(scene, reference_scene=None). The optional reference_scene is a clean-air GeoArray or plain array on the scene's pixel grid (ValueError otherwise) with the same band layout; a GeoArray reference resolves the band names against its own attrs, a plain array uses the scene's band positions. When supplied, the output is the log-ratio change.

Examples:

Reference-scene retrieval over a single source::

import geoops as gz

score = gz.plume.SBMP()(post_event_s2, pre_event_s2)
mask = gz.plume.PlumeMask(threshold="percentile:99.5")(score)
