    Returns:
        ``uint8`` array of the same shape.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``upper <= lower``.
    """
    return _unit_to_uint8(percentile_clip(arr, lower, upper, reduce_axes=reduce_axes))

docs.title: Branching pipelines
docs.text: Branch a pipeline when one chain is not enough: two scenes in, several products out, a fork on the input's type, or one recipe per sensor. Which shape to pick is in Concepts; this page builds each one.

docs.title: Combine two scenes in a Graph
docs.text:
A Graph takes several Inputs and wires them into multi-input operators. Here pre- and post-fire scenes meet at dNBR, and a threshold on the result marks the burn scar.

import numpy as np
from geoarray import GeoArray
from rasterio.transform import from_origin

import geoops as gz

rng: np.random.Generator = np.random.default_rng(0)
grid: dict = {"transform": from_origin(750_000, 4_350_000, 10, 10), "crs": "EPSG:32610"}
names: dict = {"band_names": ["B4", "B8", "B12"]}
pre: GeoArray = GeoArray(rng.uniform(0.05, 0.4, (3, 32, 32)), **grid, fill_value=np.nan, attrs=names)   # (3, 32, 32) float64
post: GeoArray = GeoArray(rng.uniform(0.05, 0.4, (3, 32, 32)), **grid, fill_value=np.nan, attrs=names)  # (3, 32, 32) float64

before: gz.Input = gz.Input("pre")
after: gz.Input = gz.Input("post")
nbr_pre: gz.Node = gz.NBR(nir="B8", swir2="B12")(before)       # (3, H, W) → (H, W) float64
nbr_post: gz.Node = gz.NBR(nir="B8", swir2="B12")(after)       # (3, H, W) → (H, W) float64
dnbr: gz.Node = gz.dNBR()(nbr_pre, nbr_post)                   # (H, W), (H, W) → (H, W) float64
burn: gz.Node = gz.Threshold(threshold=0.27)(dnbr)             # (H, W) float64 → (H, W) bool

graph: gz.Graph = gz.Graph(inputs={"pre": before, "post": after}, outputs={"dnbr": dnbr, "burn": burn})
out: dict[str, GeoArray] = graph(pre=pre, post=post)          # {"dnbr": (32, 32) float64, "burn": (32, 32) bool}

The graph checks for cycles and unreachable inputs when you build it. Each node runs once, even when several nodes read it. dNBR checks that both inputs share one pixel grid.

docs.title: Fork on the input with Branch
docs.text:
Branch(predicate, if_true, if_false) picks one of two operators per call. Here digital numbers are scaled to reflectance, and an input that is already reflectance passes through.

import numpy as np

import geoops as gz

to_reflectance: gz.Branch = gz.Branch(
    predicate=lambda x: np.issubdtype(np.asarray(x).dtype, np.integer),
    if_true=gz.DNToReflectance(scale=1e-4),
    if_false=gz.Identity(),
)
pipeline: gz.Sequential = to_reflectance | gz.NDVI(red=0, nir=1)

rng: np.random.Generator = np.random.default_rng(0)
dn: np.ndarray = rng.integers(200, 4000, size=(2, 16, 16), dtype=np.uint16)  # (2, 16, 16) uint16
refl: np.ndarray = dn * 1e-4                                                # (2, 16, 16) float64
a: np.ndarray = pipeline(dn)                                                # (2, 16, 16) uint16 → (16, 16) float64
b: np.ndarray = pipeline(refl)                                              # (2, 16, 16) float64 → (16, 16) float64
assert np.allclose(a, b)

The predicate sees the whole carrier, not each pixel. For per-pixel choices, build a mask and use gz.ApplyMask.

docs.title: Dispatch by sensor with Switch
docs.text:
Switch(key, cases, default) picks a pipeline by name. Here the band that holds near-infrared depends on the platform written in attrs.

import numpy as np
from geoarray import GeoArray
from rasterio.transform import from_origin

import geoops as gz

ndvi_by_sensor: gz.Switch = gz.Switch(
    key=lambda gt: gt.attrs["platform"],
    cases={
        "sentinel-2": gz.NDVI(red="B4", nir="B8"),
        "landsat-8": gz.NDVI(red="B4", nir="B5"),
    },
)

rng: np.random.Generator = np.random.default_rng(0)
grid: dict = {"transform": from_origin(750_000, 4_350_000, 30, 30), "crs": "EPSG:32610", "fill_value": np.nan}
s2: GeoArray = GeoArray(rng.random((2, 16, 16)), **grid, attrs={"platform": "sentinel-2", "band_names": ["B4", "B8"]})  # (2, 16, 16) float64
l8: GeoArray = GeoArray(rng.random((2, 16, 16)), **grid, attrs={"platform": "landsat-8", "band_names": ["B4", "B5"]})   # (2, 16, 16) float64

ndvi_s2: GeoArray = ndvi_by_sensor(s2)                       # (2, 16, 16) float64 → (16, 16) float64
ndvi_l8: GeoArray = ndvi_by_sensor(l8)                       # (2, 16, 16) float64 → (16, 16) float64

An unknown key runs default, which is Identity() when omitted. Pass an operator that raises if unknown sensors must fail.

docs.title: Compute several products with Fanout
docs.text:
Fanout runs one input through several operators and returns a dict. It is shorthand for a single-input Graph.

import numpy as np
from geoarray import GeoArray
from rasterio.transform import from_origin

import geoops as gz

rng: np.random.Generator = np.random.default_rng(0)
scene: GeoArray = GeoArray(
    rng.uniform(0.02, 0.5, (4, 16, 16)),                       # (4, 16, 16) float64
    transform=from_origin(750_000, 4_350_000, 10, 10), crs="EPSG:32610",
    fill_value=np.nan, attrs={"band_names": ["B3", "B4", "B8", "B12"]},
)

products: gz.Fanout = gz.Fanout({
    "ndvi": gz.NDVI(red="B4", nir="B8"),
    "ndwi": gz.NDWI(green="B3", nir="B8"),
    "nbr": gz.NBR(nir="B8", swir2="B12"),
})
out: dict[str, GeoArray] = products(scene)                   # {"ndvi", "ndwi", "nbr"}: (16, 16) float64 each

docs.title: Nest a Graph in a Sequential
docs.text:
A Graph with one input is an operator like any other. Put it after a preprocessing chain; the Sequential then returns the graph's dict.

import numpy as np

import geoops as gz

x: gz.Input = gz.Input("reflectance")
indices: gz.Graph = gz.Graph(
    inputs={"reflectance": x},
    outputs={"ndvi": gz.NDVI(red=0, nir=1)(x), "ndwi": gz.NDWI(green=2, nir=1)(x)},
)
pipeline: gz.Sequential = gz.DNToReflectance(scale=1e-4) | indices

dn: np.ndarray = np.random.default_rng(0).integers(200, 4000, size=(3, 16, 16), dtype=np.uint16)  # (3, 16, 16) uint16
out: dict[str, np.ndarray] = pipeline(dn)                     # {"ndvi", "ndwi"}: (16, 16) float64 each

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Closures do not serialise. Branch and Switch hold callables, so they are forbid_in_yaml. Rebuild such pipelines in code.
  • A terminal step ends a chain. Writers return None, so they go last; use Sink to write mid-chain.
  • Inputs must share a grid. Multi-input operators reject carriers on different grids; resample first with geom.coregister.RasterToRasterLike.

docs.title: Define an operator
docs.text: Write your own step and it composes with every built-in: in a Sequential, in a Graph, and in get_config(). This page is the one walkthrough; the model behind it is in Concepts.

docs.title: Write the operator
docs.text:
Subclass geoops.Operator (pipekit's), store each keyword-only argument under its own name, and do the work in _apply. Rewrap the result with geoops.carrier.wrap_like, or wrap_filled when nodata pixels need the output's fill, then run geoops.testing.check_operator.

import numpy as np
from geoarray import GeoArray
from rasterio.transform import from_origin

import geoops as gz
from geoops.carrier import carried_fill, wrap_filled
from geoops.testing import check_operator


class Scale(gz.Operator):
    """Multiply digital numbers by a scale factor."""

    backends = ("numpy",)                                           # it computes with NumPy

    def __init__(self, *, scale: float = 1e-4) -> None:
        self.scale = scale                                          # same name as the argument

    def _apply(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> GeoArray | np.ndarray:
        out: np.ndarray = np.asarray(gt, dtype=np.float32) * self.scale  # (C, H, W) any → (C, H, W) float32
        # Rewrap like the input and write the output's fill into its nodata pixels.
        return wrap_filled(gt, out, fill_value=carried_fill(gt, out.dtype))


rng: np.random.Generator = np.random.default_rng(0)
dn: np.ndarray = rng.integers(1, 4000, size=(4, 32, 32), dtype=np.uint16)  # (4, 32, 32) uint16
dn[:, :2, :2] = 0                                                         # a few nodata pixels
scene: GeoArray = GeoArray(
    dn, transform=from_origin(750_000, 4_350_000, 10, 10), crs="EPSG:32610",
    fill_value=0, attrs={"band_names": ["B2", "B3", "B4", "B8"]},
)

op: Scale = Scale(scale=1e-4)
reflectance: GeoArray = check_operator(op, scene)                        # (4, 32, 32) uint16 → (4, 32, 32) float32
assert op.get_config() == {"scale": 1e-4}
assert gz.Operator.from_state(op.state).get_config() == op.get_config()

check_operator fails naming the first broken rule. It checks:

  • the constructor is keyword-only, and get_config() is JSON that rebuilds an equal operator (or the operator is forbid_in_yaml);
  • the operator works on graph Input nodes;
  • a GeoArray in gives a GeoArray out on the same grid, and a plain array gives a plain array;
  • the per-band attrs keys match the output bands;
  • the fill suits the output dtype, the input's nodata stays nodata, and the input is left untouched;
  • backends is declared: a NumPy-only operator refuses a JAX carrier with pipekit_ops.BackendError, and one that lists "jax" matches its NumPy result and traces once under jax.jit;
  • a (T, C, H, W) stack matches the per-frame results, or is rejected with an error naming the operator;
  • a georeader GeoTensor is refused with a TypeError naming geoarray.interop.georeader.from_georeader (wrap_like and the nodata helpers do this for you; an operator that uses neither calls geoops.carrier.reject_geotensor).

docs.title: Follow the rules
docs.text:
Rule Why Keyword-only __init__(self, *, ...), each argument stored under its own name get_config() is derived from it; configs map to arguments by name. Hold configuration only, never a carrier A second raster is a positional _apply argument, so a Graph can wire it in. Implement _apply, never __call__ __call__ switches between eager runs and graph recording. Read with np.asarray(gt), rewrap with wrap_like Plain arrays and GeoArrays both work; CRS, transform and attrs carry over. Declare backends ("numpy",) for an _apply that reads with np.asarray; ("numpy", "jax") only when it computes with the carrier's namespace and runs under jax.jit. A carrier on another backend is refused before _apply runs, never converted. Never mutate the input The same scene may feed other branches. Declare the output fill False for masks, 0 for labels and counts, NaN for new float quantities, carried_fill(gt, dtype) for carried values. Use the shared parameter names red / nir / qa_band for one band, bands, fill_value, window, seed, eps.

The full parameter vocabulary is in packages/geotoolz-ops/AGENTS.md.

docs.title: Collapse bands and judge nodata
docs.text:
An index reads two bands and returns one value per pixel. Resolve band references by name or position, leave invalid pixels as NaN, and decorate _apply with over_frames so a (T, C, H, W) stack runs frame by frame.

import numpy as np
from geoarray import GeoArray
from rasterio.transform import from_origin

import geoops as gz
from geoops.carrier import mask_invalid_to_nan, over_frames, resolve_band, wrap_like
from geoops.testing import check_operator


class RedEdgeChlorophyll(gz.Operator):
    """CIre = NIR / red edge - 1 (Gitelson 2003); NaN where either band is nodata."""

    backends = ("numpy",)

    def __init__(self, *, nir: int | str = 3, red_edge: int | str = 2, eps: float = 1e-10) -> None:
        self.nir, self.red_edge, self.eps = nir, red_edge, eps

    @over_frames
    def _apply(self, gt: GeoArray | np.ndarray) -> GeoArray | np.ndarray:
        x: np.ndarray = mask_invalid_to_nan(gt)                       # (C, H, W) any → (C, H, W) float · NaN = nodata
        nir: np.ndarray = x[resolve_band(gt, self.nir)]               # (H, W) float
        red_edge: np.ndarray = x[resolve_band(gt, self.red_edge)]     # (H, W) float
        return wrap_like(gt, nir / (red_edge + self.eps) - 1, fill_value=np.nan)


rng: np.random.Generator = np.random.default_rng(0)
dn: np.ndarray = rng.integers(1, 4000, size=(4, 32, 32), dtype=np.uint16)  # (4, 32, 32) uint16
dn[:, :2, :2] = 0                                                         # a few nodata pixels
scene: GeoArray = GeoArray(
    dn, transform=from_origin(750_000, 4_350_000, 10, 10), crs="EPSG:32610",
    fill_value=0, attrs={"band_names": ["B2", "B4", "B5", "B8"]},
)

cire: GeoArray = check_operator(RedEdgeChlorophyll(nir="B8", red_edge="B5"), scene)  # (4, 32, 32) uint16 → (32, 32) float · NaN = nodata
assert np.isnan(np.asarray(cire)[:2, :2]).all()

Built-in indices such as gz.NDVI have the same shape. Before writing a step, search the capability index: it may already exist.

docs.title: Hold a live object
docs.text:
An operator that holds a callable, model or open handle cannot rebuild from JSON. Set forbid_in_yaml = True: its config becomes a debug repr, and from_state refuses to rebuild it.

from collections.abc import Callable

import numpy as np

import geoops as gz
from geoops.carrier import wrap_like


class ApplyFunction(gz.Operator):
    """Apply an elementwise function to every pixel."""

    forbid_in_yaml = True
    backends = ("numpy",)

    def __init__(self, *, fn: Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray]) -> None:
        self.fn = fn

    def _apply(self, gt: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        return wrap_like(gt, self.fn(np.asarray(gt)))


x: np.ndarray = np.random.default_rng(0).random((3, 8, 8))  # (3, 8, 8) float64
y: np.ndarray = ApplyFunction(fn=np.sqrt)(x)                  # (3, 8, 8) float64 → (3, 8, 8) float64

For a one-off function, pipekit's gz.Lambda(fn) does the same without a class.

docs.title: Write a terminal operator
docs.text:
An operator that returns something other than a carrier, such as None after a write, sets _terminal = True. Sequential then accepts it only as the last step.

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

import geoops as gz


class SaveNpy(gz.Operator):
    """Write the array to a .npy file; returns None."""

    _terminal = True
    backends = ("numpy",)

    def __init__(self, *, path: str) -> None:
        self.path = path

    def _apply(self, gt: np.ndarray) -> None:
        np.save(self.path, np.asarray(gt))


path: str = str(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "ndvi.npy")
x: np.ndarray = np.random.default_rng(0).random((4, 8, 8))                  # (4, 8, 8) float64
pipeline: gz.Sequential = gz.NDVI(red=2, nir=3) | SaveNpy(path=path)        # (4, 8, 8) float64 → None
pipeline(x)
saved: np.ndarray = np.load(path)                                          # (8, 8) float64

The built-in writers (gz.WriteGeoTIFF, gz.WriteCOG, gz.WriteZarr) are terminal the same way. To write mid-chain and keep the carrier flowing, use gz.Sink(write_fn), which returns its input.

docs.title: Learn state with fit and transform
docs.text:
An operator that learns from data never overwrites its constructor attributes in _apply. It follows the fitted-operator contract:

  • fit(x) -> self writes trailing-underscore attributes (mean_);
  • transform(x) only reads them;
  • _apply calls transform, after geoops.carrier.fit_once when it learns on the first call, so concurrent first calls fit once.

Fitted attributes are not constructor arguments, so they stay out of get_config() with no extra code.

class NDVIClasses(gz.Operator):
    """Label NDVI as water (1), sparse cover (2) or vegetation (3); 0 = no data.

    Args:
        water_below: NDVI under this value is water.
        vegetation_above: NDVI at or above this value is vegetation.
    """

    backends = ("numpy",)  # it computes with NumPy

    def __init__(self, *, water_below: float = 0.02, vegetation_above: float = 0.25):
        self.water_below = water_below
        self.vegetation_above = vegetation_above

    def _apply(self, ndvi: GeoArray) -> GeoArray:
        values: np.ndarray = np.asarray(ndvi)  # (..., H, W) float
        edges: list[float] = [self.water_below, self.vegetation_above]
        labels: np.ndarray = np.digitize(values, edges) + 1  # (..., H, W) int64
        labels[~np.isfinite(values)] = 0  # nodata stays nodata
        return wrap_like(ndvi, labels.astype(np.uint8), fill_value=0)
class NDVIClasses(gz.Operator): """Label NDVI as water (1), sparse cover (2) or vegetation (3); 0 = no data. docs.title: Compute — a cloud-masked NDVI pipeline over Lake Tahoe¶
docs.text:
You compose library operators into a cloud-masked NDVI pipeline, then add one operator of your own. This is step 3 of the Lake Tahoe story. The find notebook chose the scene, 2024-09-22; the cut notebook chose the 10 km South Shore box used here.

How Sequential and Graph work is explained once in Operator concepts. Here you use them on real pixels.

What you'll learn:

  1. Chain library operators with | into a Sequential.
  2. Mask cloud and shadow with gz.S2SCL and gz.ApplyMask.
  3. Wire a two-branch pipeline as a Graph.
  4. Compute several indices from one input with gz.Fanout.
  5. Write your own operator and check it with geoops.testing.check_operator.

docs.title: 1. Load the South Shore box through the catalog¶
docs.text: The scene comes from the same catalog search as the other two notebooks. Load green, red and NIR at their native 10 m, plus the 20 m scene classification layer (SCL). SCL holds class labels, so it is upsampled with nearest-neighbour resampling.

docs.title: 2. Chain operators with Sequential¶
docs.text: a | b builds a Sequential that runs a, then b. Keep the three reflectance bands, decode the stored values (reflectance × 10 000) with gz.DNToReflectance, then compute gz.NDVI.

docs.title: 3. Build a cloud mask from SCL¶
docs.text: gz.S2SCL returns a boolean mask where True means drop the pixel, the polarity every geotoolz mask uses (see Mask polarity). By default it drops every class except vegetation, bare soil and water.

docs.title: 4. Wire both branches as a Graph¶
docs.text: NDVI and the mask both start from the same scene and meet in gz.ApplyMask. A linear Sequential cannot express that, so call the operators on a symbolic gz.Input and wrap the result in a gz.Graph.

docs.title: 5. Several indices from one input with Fanout¶
docs.text: gz.Fanout runs each named operator on the same input and returns a dict. Here it adds the McFeeters water index, gz.NDWI, which uses the green band. Water has NDWI above 0, so NDWI > 0 should agree with SCL's own WATER class.

docs.title: 6. Write your own operator¶
docs.text:
The library has no NDVI land-cover classifier, so write one. Subclass gz.Operator, take keyword-only configuration, and put the work in _apply; never override __call__. Rewrap the result with geoops.carrier.wrap_like, which keeps the georeferencing and sets the new fill.

The full walkthrough is Define an operator.

docs.title: Summary¶
docs.text:
• | chained SelectBands, DNToReflectance and NDVI into one Sequential.
  • S2SCL built a drop mask (True = drop) and ApplyMask wrote NaN into it.
  • A Graph joined the NDVI and mask branches; Fanout added NDWI from the same input.
  • NDVIClasses kept the operator contract, and check_operator proved it.

Next: run this pipeline tile by tile over the whole lake with the patcher, as in the cut notebook. For runtime branching, see Branching pipelines.

docs.title: geotoolz-patcher
docs.text: Split a geospatial field into local patches, run an operator per patch, and stitch the outputs back into a global result — along four independently composable axes.

docs.title: Where it comes from
docs.text:
A model trained on 256 × 256 chips cannot see a whole Sentinel-2 tile at once, and a 1 TB output does not fit in memory. So you cut the scene into overlapping pieces, run on each, and glue the answers back without seams. Every project writes that loop again, with its own edge cases.

geopatcher splits the loop into four choices you make separately: the Geometry (the shape of a patch), the Sampler (where patches go), the Window (how each cell is weighted) and the Aggregation (how local outputs merge). Any Field goes in — a raster, an xarray grid, GeoPandas polygons, xvec points — and any per-patch callable runs. It is the patcher of the geostack; see how the packages interlock.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install geotoolz-patcher                       # base — RasterField only
pip install 'geotoolz-patcher[patch-full]'         # every Field adapter and runner
Extra Pulls in Needed for [grid] xarray geopatcher.fields.XarrayField [vector] geopandas, shapely geopatcher.fields.GeoPandasField [point] xvec geopatcher.fields.XvecField [xarray-raster] rioxarray, xarray geopatcher.fields.RioXarrayField [streaming] zarr ≥ 3 spatial.aggregation.OverlapAdd(streaming=True) [dask] dask[bag], xarray geopatcher.fields.DaskField, geopatcher.run.to_delayed [jax] geotoolz-array[jax] JAX batches: PatchBatch.patches.to_jax() after geopatcher.run.batch_split [cog] geotoolz-cloud[cog] geopatcher.fields.CogField [patch-full] all of the above everything except [pipekit] [pipekit] pipekit-ops geopatcher.integrations.pipekit (GridSampler, ApplyToChips, MergePatches)

pipekit-ops is not on PyPI yet: install the [pipekit] extra from a clone with uv sync --extra pipekit. A missing extra fails at the point of use with an ImportError that names it.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Cut a 512 × 512 raster into 128-pixel patches with 32 pixels of overlap, double each patch and stitch the result with Hann-feathered seams.

import numpy as np
import rasterio
from geoarray import GeoArray

import geopatcher as gp

# 1. Wrap a GeoArray (or any lazy geoarray.RasterSource) as a Field.
arr: np.ndarray = np.outer(np.linspace(0, 1, 512), np.linspace(0, 1, 512)).astype(np.float32)[None]  # (1, 512, 512) float32
field: gp.RasterField = gp.RasterField(
    GeoArray(arr, rasterio.Affine(10, 0, 500_000, 0, -10, 4_300_000), "EPSG:32611")
)

# 2. Compose the four axes.
patcher: gp.SpatialPatcher = gp.SpatialPatcher(
    geometry=gp.spatial.geometry.Rectangular(size=(128, 128)),
    sampler=gp.spatial.sampler.RegularStride(step=(96, 96)),        # 32 px overlap
    window=gp.spatial.window.Hann(),                                # feather the seams
    aggregation=gp.spatial.aggregation.OverlapAdd(),
)

# 3. Split → operate per patch → merge.
patches: list[gp.Patch] = list(patcher.split(field))               # 25 × GeoArray (1, 128, 128) float32
out: list[gp.Patch] = [p.with_data(np.asarray(p.data) * 2.0) for p in patches]  # 25 × (1, 128, 128) float32
stitched: np.ndarray = patcher.merge(out, field.domain)             # (1, 512, 512) float64

patch.anchor is the patch origin in pixels ((0, 0), (0, 96), …). merge returns a bare array; patcher.merge_to_field(out, field) returns a GeoArray with the source's transform and CRS. The Hann taper never reaches zero, so every covered pixel — the scene's edges included — comes back as data; see Window convention.

docs.title: Is this the right tool?
docs.text: Your job Use The operator works on the whole scene in memory the operator directly — no patcher Independent local work (inference, filters) SpatialPatcher + spatial.aggregation.OverlapAdd with a Hann or Tukey window The output is bigger than RAM OverlapAdd(streaming=True) — Stream to disk The operator needs a global statistic (scene mean / std) patcher.two_pass — Global statistics Windows along time, or space × time cubes TemporalPatcher / SpatioTemporalPatcher — Temporal patching

docs.title: Advanced — patching as a geotoolz operator
docs.text:
The [pipekit] bridge makes split → operate → merge one more Sequential, so a geotoolz operator runs tile by tile with no loop.

import numpy as np
import rasterio
from geoarray import GeoArray

import geopatcher as gp
import geoops as gz
from geoops.patch_ops import ApplyToChips, GridSampler, MergePatches

rng: np.random.Generator = np.random.default_rng(0)
scene: GeoArray = GeoArray(
    rng.integers(1, 10_000, size=(4, 512, 512), dtype=np.uint16),  # (4, 512, 512) uint16
    transform=rasterio.Affine(10, 0, 500_000, 0, -10, 4_300_000),
    crs="EPSG:32611",
    fill_value=0,
    attrs={"band_names": ["blue", "green", "red", "nir"]},
)
field: gp.RasterField = gp.RasterField(scene)
patcher: gp.SpatialPatcher = gp.SpatialPatcher(
    geometry=gp.spatial.geometry.Rectangular(size=(128, 128)),
    sampler=gp.spatial.sampler.RegularStride(step=(96, 96)),
    window=gp.spatial.window.Hann(),
    aggregation=gp.spatial.aggregation.OverlapAdd(),
)

ndvi: gz.Sequential = gz.DNToReflectance(scale=1e-4) | gz.NDVI(nir="nir", red="red")
tiled: gz.Sequential = gz.Sequential([
    GridSampler(patcher=patcher),          # field → 25 Patches     (4, 128, 128) uint16
    ApplyToChips(operator=ndvi),           # (4, 128, 128) uint16 → (128, 128) float64
    MergePatches(aggregation=gp.spatial.aggregation.OverlapAdd(), domain=field.domain),
])
ndvi_map: GeoArray = tiled(field)          # (512, 512) float64 · NaN = no data

The domain fixes the grid and the patches fix the bands, so NDVI's one-band chips merge into one (H, W) map on the scene's transform and CRS. The stack quickstart runs the same pipeline on real Sentinel-2 data.
